skills.name: Durability
skills.summary: The tank.
skills.quiet: You're still standing. Of course you are.
skills.notices: That beam would hold your weight. Probably. It's held worse than you.

ep.speaker: Sanchez of the Burning Bridge
quote: Yeah, I take hits for a living. Men these days are weak one way or another, and I mostly make my money off the ones who are weak in the heart.
ep.intro: Durability is your metabolism and circulation; what commoners call "being in good shape." Who cares if you can shoot fire from your palms when you can inhale the fireball they just threw and breathe it back in their faces?
ep.effect: Your Guard pool holds 1 more (5 at most). The Guard technique gives you more Guard: 1, plus 1 for every point here after the first (Brace gives a flat 2, whatever your points).
ep.high: you look like a pro wrestler and weaker folk start trembling. Not sure they'll dare talk to a walking marble statue, though.
ep.good: gym rats, tomboys, brawlers who tank for the team.
ep.bad: scholars, exam crammers, light-armour fans.

perks.name: Stonewall
perks.t1: Allies standing directly behind you, in line with the attacker, take 25% less damage from ranged attacks.
perks.t2: Allies up to 2 tiles directly behind you, in line with the attacker, take 50% less damage from ranged attacks.

perks.name: Shrug It Off
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to remove one Body debuff from yourself.
perks.t2: Spend 1 AP to remove one Body debuff from yourself and gain a shield worth 10% of your max HP.

mastered.name: Last Wall
mastered.flavour: The wall doesn't fall. The wall decides when it's done.
mastered.text: Once per fight, a hit that would drop you to 0 HP leaves you at 1 HP instead, and you take no damage at all until your next turn starts. Damage you do to yourself doesn't trigger it.

combos.name: Siege Engine
combos.text: Shove and the Break Finisher cost you 1 AP less, never below 1 AP. A Shove that moves its target gives you 1 Guard. Nothing can push you or knock you back.
combos.deed: Break through a wall to win a fight.

skills.name: Pain Threshold
skills.summary: Wounds don't slow you down.
skills.quiet: Something stung you a while back. Nothing to worry about. Probably.
skills.notices: The burn on your hand is real. You'll want to look at it later.

ep.speaker: Sazmin of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Want to test if your poison's strong enough? Coat a blade and go poke Knight Jiren in the arm. No, I'm serious. Once he sleepwalked into the snake pen, slept there all night and walked out with a dozen Crobar still hanging off his back. THEN HE WENT AND MADE BREAKFAST. Sometimes I wonder if anyone around here is still normal.
ep.intro: Pain Threshold is why you can take an arrow and still get up. Or change a lightbulb without flipping the breaker? Who knows. Just remember: not feeling pain doesn't mean you can't die. Don't get delusional.
ep.effect: −10% elemental damage taken. +2 HP every level.
ep.high: the "threshold" part disappears and you go numb to anything that hurts. And again: A KNIFE YOU CAN'T FEEL CAN STILL STOP YOUR HEART.
ep.good: bushido duellists the sneaky types keep poisoning, people who hate pain, the last survivor of a house fire, masochists.
ep.bad: anyone who still likes their limbs and doesn't want to lose one because they "forgot fire is hot."

perks.name: Used to the Pain
perks.t1: The first time you are hit in each fight: if that hit took less than 20% of your max HP, the next hit against you deals 25% less damage. A heavier first hit gives you nothing.
perks.t2: The first time you are hit in each fight: if that hit took less than 30% of your max HP, the next hit against you deals 40% less damage. A heavier first hit gives you nothing.

perks.name: Scar Tissue
perks.t1: Each hit that wounds you in a fight gives you 5% less Elemental damage taken for the rest of that fight, up to 25%.
perks.t2: Each hit that wounds you in a fight gives you 5% less Elemental damage taken and +5% Injury resistance for the rest of that fight, up to 40% each.

mastered.name: Walking Wounded
mastered.flavour: Hurt is information. You've read it all before.
mastered.text: Injuries never cost you AP or Movement: a head injury doesn't Daze you and a leg injury doesn't slow you. While you are below half your max HP, you take 20% less damage.

combos.name: Bite the Bullet
combos.text: Once per fight, when you would drop to 0 HP, you stay on your feet until the end of your next turn (or of this turn, if it is yours). Until then every hit you take is a failed death save instead of damage. At the end of it you go Downed, unless you have been healed.
combos.deed: Fight through an entire combat below a quarter of your max HP.

skills.name: Senses
skills.summary: Touch, smell, temperature and the ground under your feet. Not sight or sound; that's Vigilance.
skills.quiet: Rain's coming. You can feel it in the knuckles.
skills.notices: The floor is warmer by the far wall. Something runs behind it.

ep.speaker: Sister March of the Lumeri Church
quote: She can feel it, trust me. Even a single sigh. Back when her eyes still worked and her legs hadn't given out, Grandma Marry was already the Grandma Marry she is now. What I always admired most was how she could read the temperature of the air with one finger raised to the sky. Or the way she sits in her deck chair, eyes closed, smelling the morning, with a smile on her lips. Sometimes she makes a twenty-year-old girl like me jealous.
ep.intro: Sensory is how sensitive your skin and senses are to the world: a cold breeze, a scent you can't name, a faint tremor underground. With high Sensory it feels like nature itself is shaking your hand.
ep.effect: You sense what you can't see (by ear, smell and touch) 1 better. Your Warn Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you become one with every movement around you, a little too well. If your ears are that sharp, stay away from concerts. Those speakers don't hit gently.
ep.good: people who stroll for the breeze, travellers who go somewhere just to breathe it, scouts and rogues listening for footsteps.
ep.bad: death metal fans, people who can't take the cold, elves of every kind.

perks.name: Wind on the Skin
perks.t1: When a fight starts, your squad learns where the nearest enemy it can't see within your Vision range is. You know its tile, but you still can't target it.
perks.t2: When a fight starts, your squad learns where every enemy it can't see within your Vision range is. You know their tiles, but you still can't target them.

perks.name: Bedside Manner
perks.t1: In a conversation, touch someone (a handshake, a hand on the shoulder). The Narrator tells you privately whether the next thing they say is a lie.
perks.t2: In a conversation, touch someone (a handshake, a hand on the shoulder). The Narrator tells you privately whether the next thing they say is a lie, whether they are afraid, and of whom.

mastered.name: Skin Map
mastered.flavour: The air moves around them. The floor remembers their weight. You don't need eyes.
mastered.text: No enemy within 6 tiles can stay Hidden from you. Darkness, smoke and invisibility don't stop you sensing it, though walls still do, and your own shots within 6 tiles ignore smoke.

combos.name: Sixth Sense
combos.text: Hidden enemies within 3 tiles of you are revealed to you and your whole squad, even through walls.
combos.deed: Catch someone tailing the squad before they strike.

skills.name: Raw Power
skills.summary: Hit harder, bend further, lift higher.
skills.quiet: Your arms are the cleverest thing about you, and that's fine.
skills.notices: The hinges are weaker than the door. Hit those.

ep.speaker: Knight Andre "Giant Fist" of the Adamantile Brigade
quote: Back in the army they kept saying my arms were bigger than my brain. Yeah, maybe. Maybe. If I pulled my brain out and measured it with a ruler, my arm probably is bigger. But you can't arm-wrestle with a brain, and when it comes to arm-wrestling I'm the best there is. So I used my arms to wrestle their brains, and a few concrete tables. Nobody said anything after that.
ep.intro: Just saying the name makes you feel the strength rising. Raw Power isn't technique, calm or authority. It's STRENGTH: hit harder, bend further, lift higher. Things only muscle can do.
ep.effect: +1 to hit with heavy melee weapons and bare hands. +5% physical damage. Your melee techniques are harder to save against. From 2 points, +1 to your counter-attacks.
ep.high: you break locks, doors and bones, and laugh at people who can't. But that much muscle makes it easy to hurt the things you never meant to.
ep.good: martial artists, berserkers, competitive lifters, guys going for the record on the bar's punching machine.
ep.bad: mages, cat and bunny lovers, high nobility who don't want to be called thugs.

perks.name: Breaching Strike
perks.t1: When one of your melee techniques pushes a target and a wall, a solid object or another enemy stops it, the target takes the hit again at half damage.
perks.t2: When one of your melee techniques pushes a target and a wall, a solid object or another enemy stops it, the target takes the hit again at half damage. An enemy it was pushed into takes that damage too.

perks.name: Iron Grip
perks.t1: You gain the technique Grapple: for 1 AP, an enemy next to you makes a Body save or is Grappled. A target you have Grappled or Bound can't use Answers or reactions, and attacks aimed at you have a 50% chance to hit it instead. When you move, you drag it with you.
perks.t2: You gain the technique Grapple: for 1 AP, an enemy next to you makes a Body save or is Grappled. A target you have Grappled or Bound can't use Answers or reactions, attacks aimed at you have a 50% chance to hit it instead, and when you move you drag it with you. Each of your melee techniques that hits a target you hold gives you 1 Momentum, and Throw Down on it needs no Momentum.

mastered.name: Earthbreaker
mastered.flavour: They took cover. You took the cover.
mastered.text: Once per fight, spend 4 AP to strike the ground at a tile within your melee reach. Everyone else in the 3×3 area around it, allies included, takes your melee damage with no roll and is knocked Prone. All cover and breakable objects in that area are destroyed.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 4 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Siege Engine
combos.text: Shove and the Break Finisher cost you 1 AP less, never below 1 AP. A Shove that moves its target gives you 1 Guard. Nothing can push you or knock you back.
combos.deed: Break through a wall to win a fight.

skills.name: Guts
skills.summary: Fear doesn't get a vote.
skills.quiet: Hold your breath. Walk in. That's the whole secret.
skills.notices: The others are scared of the noise, not the room. The room is quiet.

ep.speaker: Ragoul the Keeper
quote: Why has no one else uncovered the secret of Arganzaz? Because they are a pack of faint hearts, that's why. I saw a jade-inlaid door twenty yards wide slowly opening. I heard a thousand wandering ghosts wailing and smelled ten thousand walking corpses. What they did was scream and run. What I did was hold my breath and walk in. That is why they now call me the Keeper of the secret of Arganzaz.
ep.intro: Guts is your tolerance for anything spooky or scary: a door with a skull over it, or a pitch-black hole with a sign saying "Hole of Pain." What it is doesn't matter. What matters is that you're not scared of it.
ep.effect: +1 on Body saves (poison, knock-downs, being pushed or pinned).
ep.high: you feel like an impregnable fortress. But people don't label things "dangerous" for fun, and you not being scared doesn't stop it from chewing your bones.
ep.good: thrill-seekers, manly men, manly women, holo-streamers filming viral reels in abandoned graveyards.
ep.bad: horror-movie fans, delicate ladies, team leaders and scouts.

perks.name: Into the Dark
perks.t1: The first time in a fight you move onto ground your squad hasn't seen, you can't be ambushed: until your next turn starts, attacks from hiding get no Ambush bonus against you.
perks.t2: The first time in a fight you move onto ground your squad hasn't seen, you can't be ambushed: until your next turn starts, attacks from hiding get no Ambush bonus against you. You also can't be made Afraid during the first round of a fight in a place that causes Fear.

perks.name: Iron Stomach
perks.t1: Nausea and Fear last at most 1 round on you.
perks.t2: You are immune to Nausea and Fear.

mastered.name: Nothing Left to Fear
mastered.flavour: You've already met the worst thing. It blinked first.
mastered.text: You are immune to Fear. Allies within 3 tiles who can see you can't be made Afraid, and an ally who starts a turn there stops being Afraid.

combos.name: Bite the Bullet
combos.text: Once per fight, when you would drop to 0 HP, you stay on your feet until the end of your next turn (or of this turn, if it is yours). Until then every hit you take is a failed death save instead of damage. At the end of it you go Downed, unless you have been healed.
combos.deed: Fight through an entire combat below a quarter of your max HP.

skills.name: Intimidation
skills.summary: You run the conversation through fear.
skills.quiet: Manners first. Then the bones.
skills.notices: He keeps touching his collar. He's already afraid; you only have to agree with him.

ep.speaker: Tommy Avencio, the "Papa" of the Smetanita Conjunction
quote: Have you ever had the pleasure of tasting animal marrow? Oh, who am I kidding. A merchant from Mandestra must have tasted every pleasure under the sun. Forgive my peasant manners. And you know what, Mr. Galon? If the shipment I'm waiting for doesn't arrive on time, then with these two peasant hands I'll treat you to a very special marrow broth, made from the bones of your arm. Understand? Snap that dainty hand of yours like a chicken neck, and then we savour that faintly sweet flavour together, like business partners sharing a milkshake. Slurp. Slurp. Slurp.
ep.intro: Intimidation is your control over the fear of whoever stands in front of you. One piercing look, one commanding cough: the person running this conversation is you.
ep.effect: Your Threaten Call reaches 1 tile further and is harder to shake off. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: everyone sees a demon in human skin, whether you want it or not. Whether that's good or bad is up to you.
ep.good: people done with smooth talkers' bullshit, people who want every conversation to open with the other guy's trousers turning brown, serial killers.
ep.bad: upstanding middle-class citizens, anyone keeping an angelic image, heartbreakers.

perks.name: Grim Reaper
perks.t1: You have 1 AP less on your first turn of each fight. When you kill or knock out an enemy on your own turn, you gain 2 AP. Once every 3 turns.
perks.t2: When you kill or knock out an enemy on your own turn, you gain 2 AP. Once every 3 turns. Each time you do, every enemy who sees it makes a Heart save or is Afraid of you.

perks.name: Bone Talk
perks.t1: Threaten someone with one specific, physical detail. Outside a fight they answer one question truthfully, or refuse and are Shaken; the Narrator plays the answer. In a fight it costs 2 AP: one enemy within 8 tiles who can see you makes a Heart save or is Shaken.
perks.t2: Threaten a whole group with one specific, physical detail. Outside a fight their leader answers one question truthfully for all of them, or they refuse and are all Shaken; the Narrator plays the answer. In a fight it costs 2 AP: every enemy within 8 tiles who can see you makes a Heart save or is Shaken.

mastered.name: The Name They Whisper
mastered.flavour: They tell stories about you to keep their recruits in line.
mastered.text: When a fight starts, every enemy makes a Heart save or is Afraid of you for 2 rounds. Only a stranger is spared: the Narrator says who has never heard of you. An enemy at half HP or less that can see you makes a Heart save at the end of its turn or surrenders. That works once per enemy, only while you are standing, and never on a boss.

combos.name: Charge!
combos.text: Once per turn, when you move 3 or more tiles in a straight line and end next to an enemy you can see, up to 3 AP of that move is free.
combos.deed: Open a fight by charging the enemy line, and win it.

combos.name: Make Way
combos.text: Moving past enemies never draws opportunity attacks from them; Overwatch can still fire. Crowds part for you: bystanders don't block your path, and the Narrator plays the rest.
combos.deed: Walk through a hostile crowd with no weapon drawn.

skills.name: Dexterity
skills.summary: The quick hand. Guns, bows, thrown weapons and light blades; reloads, recoil, quick-draw.
skills.quiet: Breathe. Count the rounds. You have four.
skills.notices: His holster's cut for a left-hand draw. Watch the left.

ep.speaker: Ambrosius Costeau, the Old Drifter
quote: No tricks here. I don't even need to open my eyes. I've carried this revolver since the years before Operation Daggerfall, stranger. Call me old-fashioned, call me outdated, but don't take this old body lightly in a gunfight. Wander within 500 metres and if your head doesn't vanish, your hat will need a big patch. These eyes aren't what they were, but these hands have never left the gunbelt. Identify. Squeeze. Breathe the powder smoke. Dig the grave.
ep.intro: Dexterity measures how reliable you are at anything that needs precision. Anyone can reload a gun or throw a dart. Nobody does it as fast or as clean as you.
ep.effect: +1 to hit with guns, light blades and thrown weapons. +2% critical damage. You throw half a tile further. Your shots' techniques are harder to save against.
ep.high: your hands work like a machine and your trained skills fire almost on their own. So you want to use them even when it's the wrong moment, and announcing your habits to the whole world is never a good idea.
ep.good: gunslingers, snipers, blade masters, point strikers.
ep.bad: gamblers, magic users, anyone who doesn't want to be called "hands faster than brain."

perks.name: Both Hands
perks.t1: After one of your melee techniques hits, your next shot that turn has no Recoil.
perks.t2: After one of your melee techniques hits, your next shot that turn has no Recoil. Once per turn, when one of your shots hits, you gain 1 Momentum.

perks.name: Running Reload
perks.t1: Once per turn, you can reload as part of a move, for no extra AP.
perks.t2: Once per turn, you can reload as part of a move, for no extra AP. Once per turn, you can also clear a jam as part of a move.

mastered.name: Trick Shot
mastered.flavour: Off the pipe, off the plate, into the second one. You called it.
mastered.text: Once per turn, you can make a ranged attack a Ricochet. It ignores half cover, and if it hits, the nearest other enemy within 2 tiles of the target takes half the damage the target took.

combos.name: Dance of Iron
combos.text: When an attack against you misses, you fire one shot back at the attacker for 0 AP. This uses your reaction, and you need a loaded ranged weapon with the attacker in sight and in range.
combos.deed: Dodge three attacks in one round.

skills.name: Athletics
skills.summary: Armour just slows you down.
skills.quiet: Light on your feet. They swing like Orks; you move like you.
skills.notices: There's a ledge under the window. Two steps and you're out of their line.

ep.speaker: Dominik Edelgard, the "Banner Lord" of the 237th Hellraiser Division
quote: Armour? What armour? Oh, I left the vest at base. First-floor locker room, locker 16, key's under the red flowerpot if you want it. Natalia still grumbles every time I deploy: 'Are those two banners on your back for a burial shroud or what?' But the armoury boys lean on tech way too much. What I'm fighting out here are Orks. ORKS. They swing junk machetes, and the gunners aren't any better, aiming with both eyes open. If you can dodge everything they throw at you, armour just slows you down!
ep.intro: Athletics is how nimble and supple you are. It decides how well you pull off anything that needs flexibility: flips, swimming, dodging.
ep.effect: +1 Defense (you are harder to hit), from 2 points.
ep.high: your body is light as a feather and limber as a cat. Until someone ties you down. Then you aren't a person who lost a leg, you're a bird that lost its wings. Prepare for the trauma.
ep.good: gymnasts, dancers, guys who spam crouch after every kill.
ep.bad: slow-living types, high nobility, heavy-armour users.

perks.name: Wall Run
perks.t1: During a move you can run along walls, over low obstacles and across gaps, up to 2 such tiles in a row. The move must end on open floor.
perks.t2: During a move you can run along walls, over low obstacles and across gaps, up to 4 such tiles in a row. With Wall Run strike you can attack once from the middle of the run; the move and the attack cost their usual AP. The move must end on open floor.

perks.name: Roll With It
perks.t1: Once per round, when an attack against you misses, move 1 tile for free. The move draws no opportunity attacks. If the miss comes on an enemy's turn, you take the free move on your next turn.
perks.t2: Once per round, when an attack against you misses, move up to 2 tiles for free. The move draws no opportunity attacks. If the miss comes on an enemy's turn, you take the free move on your next turn.

mastered.name: Never There
mastered.flavour: Aim where they'll be. They won't be there either.
mastered.text: Your first move each turn draws no opportunity attacks and no Overwatch. On any later move that turn, ranged attacks made against you as you move are at −4 to hit.

combos.name: Charge!
combos.text: Once per turn, when you move 3 or more tiles in a straight line and end next to an enemy you can see, up to 3 AP of that move is free.
combos.deed: Open a fight by charging the enemy line, and win it.

combos.name: Dance of Iron
combos.text: When an attack against you misses, you fire one shot back at the attacker for 0 AP. This uses your reaction, and you need a loaded ranged weapon with the attacker in sight and in range.
combos.deed: Dodge three attacks in one round.

skills.name: Reaction Speed
skills.summary: Spotting danger is one thing. Moving in time is another.
skills.quiet: You're fast. Fast isn't the same as right.
skills.notices: Glint on the rooftop. Left. Now.

ep.speaker: Yukimura of the Black Scavengers
quote: I shoot first. Honestly, you don't need fancy gear out here. Want it harder? Hand me a couple of daggers. Surviving the lowlands is tough because it has the one thing the desert doesn't: dead buildings. Wherever you go in here, you're swimming through a concrete forest. If they poke out of some dark corner and you don't react in time, a hundred percent you end up strung on a pole. Me, I just throw a knife and duck before they pull the trigger.
ep.intro: Reaction Speed is the time between your eyes firing and your body moving: a glint from an enemy scope, or a strange blink from a partner right before the handshake. Spotting danger is one thing. Reacting in time is another.
ep.effect: +1 Initiative: you act earlier in the round. Your Cue Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you're frighteningly fast and never caught flat-footed. But reacting that fast makes you look plainly impatient, and plenty of times reacting fast just makes things go wrong faster.
ep.good: gamers, sailors, gunners, every other kind of -er, gamblers.
ep.bad: calm people, people who need to save face, anyone who doesn't want to look like they're on speed.

perks.name: Rounding Up
perks.t1: Once per turn, when a cost leaves you with a fraction of an AP (drawing a glyph, for example), your AP rounds up to the next whole point.
perks.t2: Once per turn, when a cost leaves you with a fraction of an AP (drawing a glyph, for example), your AP rounds up to the next whole point. Once per fight, 1 AP you didn't spend carries over into your next turn.

perks.name: Catch
perks.t1: When a grenade or a thrown weapon is thrown at you or at an ally next to you, you catch it and it doesn't go off. This uses your reaction. On your turn you can throw it back for 1 AP; if you still hold it at the end of your next turn, it goes off in your hands.
perks.t2: When a grenade or a thrown weapon is thrown at you or at an ally next to you, you catch it and it doesn't go off. This uses your reaction. On your turn you can throw it back for 0 AP; if you still hold it at the end of your next turn, it goes off in your hands.

mastered.name: Before the Blink
mastered.flavour: Initiative is a polite word for who was faster. That was you.
mastered.text: You always act first in round 1, whatever you rolled for initiative. You have 2 reactions each round instead of 1.

combos.name: Between Heartbeats
combos.text: Once per fight, when an enemy you can see starts an action, you act first with 2 free AP: a shot at it, a move, dropping Prone, a stim for an ally next to you, or a reload. You choose which on your turn, and it waits until an enemy sets it off. It doesn't use your reaction.
combos.deed: Come through an ambush without being hit.

skills.name: Ingenuity
skills.summary: Stealth, sleight of hand, sticky fingers.
skills.quiet: Nobody is watching the back stairs. Nobody ever is.
skills.notices: The guard's keys are on the left hip, and he's tired.

ep.speaker: Lin Shin Long
quote: A thousand gold for two rocks. The number of people still paying in gold coins outside Central City is baffling. Back when I worked the city, I'd swipe a bank card out of some guy's pocket and that was dinner sorted. Back then I still had Travis to crack the cards... People call it petty theft, but the trade takes real skill. First you learn to walk in step with the crowd and spot which pocket bulges most. Then you work out how much weight to slip back in so they don't notice the coins have flown. If you don't know how, don't mess around. The old men at the guard post started carrying shock batons last week, and it hurts like you wouldn't believe.
ep.intro: Ingenuity is the finesse in everything you do: staying unseen while sneaking, picking pockets, that sort of thing.
ep.effect: +5% ambush damage. Every 2 points, enemies need 1 more to spot you while you sneak. Your traps and poisons are harder to save against.
ep.high: you turn into a cosplayer of the sneaking-soldier legend, flickering in and out of the shadows. But all that shifty behaviour makes it hard to look a cop in the eye.
ep.good: rogues, scouts, bandits, gamblers.
ep.bad: model citizens, uniformed (not undercover) cops, anyone trying to romance a uniformed (not undercover) cop.

perks.name: Sleight of Hand
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to plant an item from your pack on a target next to you without being seen; not in the middle of a conversation. A grenade goes off at the start of the target's next turn, and a tracker leaves it Marked for the rest of the fight. The Narrator decides what anything else (evidence, say) leads to.
perks.t2: Spend 1 AP to plant an item from your pack on a target next to you without being seen, even in the middle of a conversation. A grenade goes off at the start of the target's next turn, and a tracker leaves it Marked for the rest of the fight. The Narrator decides what anything else (evidence, say) leads to.

perks.name: Shadow Step
perks.t1: While you are Hidden, a move from a tile next to cover to another tile next to cover counts as half as many tiles (rounded up), so it costs less AP.
perks.t2: While you are Hidden, a move from a tile next to cover to another tile next to cover counts as half as many tiles (rounded up), so it costs less AP. When one of your attacks would reveal you, roll Ingenuity against the enemies who can see you: on a success you stay Hidden. Each success makes the next roll in that fight harder.

mastered.name: Vanishing Act
mastered.flavour: Everyone saw you. Nobody can say where you went.
mastered.text: Once per fight, spend 2 AP to become Hidden where you stand, even in plain view. You stay Hidden until you attack, shove or release an Outburst, take damage, or an enemy ends its move next to you.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 2 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Just the Repairman
combos.text: While you carry a toolbox: when someone spots you sneaking, there is a 50% chance they take you for maintenance staff and you stay hidden from them. They don't look again that scene unless you attack.
combos.deed: Talk your way past a guard who caught you somewhere you shouldn't be.

combos.name: Silent Partner
combos.text: When you hide, one ally next to you becomes Hidden with you. They lose it when they end a move away from you, or when you are found.
combos.deed: Get the whole squad through a guarded area unseen.

combos.name: Dead Signal
combos.text: While you are Hidden or no enemy can see you, spend 1 AP to silently disable one electronic device within 3 tiles: a lamp goes dark, a lock opens, a camera, alarm, terminal or turret stops working.
combos.deed: Shut down a security system without anyone noticing.

skills.name: Acuity
skills.summary: Seeing how a thing works: a lock, a mechanism, a crime scene, an enemy. Analyze (2 AP) reveals one enemy's HP, armour, resistances and weak points.
skills.quiet: Every piece fits somewhere. You just have to see all of them.
skills.notices: That turret's feed is jammed on the third link. It's firing half as often as it should.

ep.speaker: Demitri Kortev of Kortev Utility Shack
quote: Yes, yes, a watchmaker and a gunsmith aren't far apart. Lay every part of a pendulum clock on the table and odds are your brain starts shorting out. Guns are the same: picking one up and shooting is a world away from stripping every screw and putting it back. Anyone can read a clock, but how many can fix one? What you need is someone who sees every piece of the puzzle and joins them into one. Like me! Unless you use a digital clock or one of those toy guns from the carnival stalls, in which case: scram. Shoo, shoo.
ep.intro: Acuity is your grasp of complex mechanisms, from something as small as a stopwatch to something as huge as a transcontinental cannon. All of it can be taken apart by you.
ep.effect: −5% critical damage taken. Analyse reaches 1 tile further; at 3 points it is quicker (Quick Read), and at 5 it also shows the target's weak point.
ep.high: you see how everything works, man-made or not: a lock, a network, a crime scene, the way an enemy guards itself. That helps with a lot, but the first answer that fits is the one you keep, and you lose interest in anything that can't be taken apart, people included.
ep.good: detectives, locksmiths, slicers, clockmakers, anyone who reads an enemy before the shooting starts.
ep.bad: enchanters, party people, therapists, anyone who has to act before they understand.

perks.name: Detective's Eye
perks.t1: In every scene, the Narrator tells you one detail that is out of place. When a fight starts, you spot one hidden trap or one enemy's weak point for free.
perks.t2: In every scene, the Narrator tells you two details that are out of place, and whether they are connected. When a fight starts, you spot two hidden traps or enemy weak points for free.

perks.name: Pattern Lock
perks.t1: You have +2 Defense against any kind of attack you have already seen in this fight: the same weapon used the same way.
perks.t2: You have +4 Defense against any kind of attack you have already seen in this fight: the same weapon used the same way. While you are standing, your allies have +2 Defense against those attacks too.

mastered.name: Case Closed
mastered.flavour: Everything about them, in the order it matters.
mastered.text: Your Analyze reveals everything at once: HP, Defense, armour, resistances, saves, conditions and weak points, and the Narrator tells you what the target wants. You and your allies have +2 Defense against an enemy you have analyzed, and deal 20% more damage to it.

combos.name: Cold Read
combos.text: Whenever you Analyze someone, the Narrator also tells you privately what they want most.
combos.deed: Close a case with a confession.

combos.name: Dead Signal
combos.text: While you are Hidden or no enemy can see you, spend 1 AP to silently disable one electronic device within 3 tiles: a lamp goes dark, a lock opens, a camera, alarm, terminal or turret stops working.
combos.deed: Shut down a security system without anyone noticing.

skills.name: Vigilance
skills.summary: Sight, sound and hostile intent.
skills.quiet: Your spine went cold a second ago. Listen to it.
skills.notices: Two men in the doorway; one is pretending to drink.

ep.speaker: Vermilion Jasmine of Rigaz Trade Company (RTC™®)
quote: They keep saying I can dodge bullets. As if any human could. They've got a few knives in the neck before they can pull the trigger, that's all. Run enough jobs for old Rourigaz and you'll get used to it: every time someone aims at you, even from the dark, your spine goes cold. Just remember to cut their spine out in return, as a thank-you gift.
ep.intro: Vigilant is the survival instinct your ancestors handed down. An enemy in the bushes, a prying gaze in the dark: with eyes and ears tuned to detail, you notice what's off before anyone else.
ep.effect: You notice traps, hidden things and hidden enemies 1 better, and 1 tile further off. Your Spot Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you're hyper-aware of everything you see and hear and can sense danger in a heartbeat. But that alert, you're never sure if the danger is real or you're just imagining things.
ep.good: debtors on the run from loan sharks, husbands afraid of wives in high heels, grunts terrified of punji traps, snipers.
ep.bad: anyone who doesn't want to be called jumpy or a coward.

perks.name: Got You in My Sight
perks.t1: When an enemy you can see hides or leaves your sight, you gain 2 AP: at once on your own turn, or on your coming turn if you have not acted yet this round. If your turn this round is already over, you gain nothing. Once every 3 turns. When an Ambush hits you, you have 2 AP less on your next turn; that too happens at most once every 3 turns.
perks.t2: When an enemy you can see hides or leaves your sight, you gain 2 AP: at once on your own turn, or on your coming turn if you have not acted yet this round. If your turn this round is already over, you gain nothing. Once every 3 turns. Your squad always knows where that enemy was last seen.

perks.name: Eyes in the Back
perks.t1: You can't be flanked. Half cover next to you, and a shield you carry, protect you against ranged attacks from every direction.
perks.t2: You and the allies next to you can't be flanked. Half cover next to any of you, and a carried shield, protect its owner against ranged attacks from every direction.

mastered.name: Nothing Gets Past
mastered.flavour: You held the line of sight. All of it.
mastered.text: Every enemy that moves in your sight is Spotted for free, exactly as your Spot Call would mark it. It costs no AP and no reaction, and works once per round on each enemy. It doesn't work while you are Silenced or Stunned.

combos.name: Sixth Sense
combos.text: Hidden enemies within 3 tiles of you are revealed to you and your whole squad, even through walls.
combos.deed: Catch someone tailing the squad before they strike.

skills.name: Brain Power
skills.summary: Raw processing speed for Sigils. Attack skill for Sigils that strike.
skills.quiet: Breathe. Draw the path in your head first. Then the hand.
skills.notices: The sigil burned blue, not white: a CONDENSE was drawn twice. Someone here is sloppy.

ep.speaker: Professor Avdol of the Science Team
quote: Stop flailing and concentrate. In nearly twenty years of using an Evoker I have never needed to dance a single kata to trigger a sigil. If you want martial arts in your magic, kindly go south and join a sect. I may be a spellcaster, but I am a scientist and they are philosophers. Now breathe deep, memorise the sigil's path, draw it, and press the blue button on the right-hand grip. If you burn through your MagiCore before finishing a Fireball, I'm done teaching you.
ep.intro: Brain Power is your brain's processing speed. In PC-parts terms, it's the difference between two graphics cards. It lets you handle information faster than others, and helps a lot with Sigils and Evokers.
ep.effect: +10% Sigil power. You know 1 more Sigil word. Every 2 points: Sigils reach 1 tile further and last 1 round longer. Every 3 points: a Sigil burns 1 less core charge. Your Sigils' conditions are harder to save against.
ep.high: your brain is always hunting detail, almost hyperactive. Look at a rock and instead of "where's it from" and "why is it here", you're on "its chemical composition" and "a hundred ways to arrange rocks into a code." Training a brain that big isn't always smart.
ep.good: Evoker users, scientists, researchers.
ep.bad: Emanator users, healers, melee fighters.

perks.name: Hold the Stroke
perks.t1: You can keep 1 more of your glyphs on the ground at once before the oldest fades.
perks.t2: You can keep 2 more of your glyphs on the ground at once before the oldest fades.

perks.name: Parallel Thought
perks.t1: Once per turn, while one of your placed spells still stands (a field, a trap or a turret), your next Sigil spell costs 1 AP less: off its glyphs first, then off its Evoke.
perks.t2: Once per turn, while one of your placed spells still stands (a field, a trap or a turret), your next Sigil spell costs 2 AP less: off its glyphs first, then off its Evoke.

mastered.name: Clean Draw
mastered.flavour: No charge, no smoke, no Flux. Just the shape, perfectly.
mastered.text: Once per fight, for 0 AP, make your next Sigil spell a clean one. The glyphs you draw for it (up to 4) cost no Core charge and add no Flux, and Evoking it costs no charge either.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: Spend 2 AP to explain one visible enemy's weakness so simply that anyone can use it. Every ally within 6 tiles gets +2 to hit that enemy until your next turn starts.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

skills.name: Rumination
skills.summary: The scientist's library. Mirrors Lore Master.
skills.quiet: You have read about this. Page forty, or thereabouts.
skills.notices: That banner is from the second Daggerfall levy. Those units were disbanded for mutiny.

ep.speaker: Thalatûl the Librarian
quote: The knowledge you need to become a Keeper of Books? Seven hundred and forty-five reigns. Two hundred thousand years of history. Five hundred and forty thousand inventions, great and small. Nine million three hundred and fifty thousand species of plant and animal, and hundreds of millions of pages turned. Now kindly erase your presence from my library.
ep.intro: Rumination is how well you absorb and retain scientific knowledge: history, politics, maths, physics, chemistry. It also lets you look at an object and pull up the theory behind it.
ep.effect: +1 on Brain saves (confusion, illusions, having your mind turned).
ep.high: you always side with science, experiment and hard data. Great in a lab; uncomfortable with anything science can't explain, like incantations, charms, souls or spiritual links.
ep.good: bookworms, hackermen, tech professionals of every field.
ep.bad: lifters who only care about strength, students of the surreal, the devout, conspiracy preachers on the pirate bands.

perks.name: Footnote
perks.t1: Once per scene, cite a fact: allies who act on it get +1 on that roll, and the Narrator decides which rolls count. In a fight, once per fight and for 0 AP, cite a fact about one enemy: your allies get +1 to hit it for the rest of the round.
perks.t2: Once per scene, cite a fact: allies who act on it get +2 on that roll, and the Narrator decides which rolls count. In a fight, once per fight and for 0 AP, cite a fact about one enemy: your allies get +2 to hit it for the rest of the round.

perks.name: Lab Coat
perks.t1: You have +3 on saves against chemicals, gases and drugs you have identified.
perks.t2: You have +3 on saves against chemicals, gases and drugs you have identified. Spend 2 AP (free outside a fight) to neutralise one of them for allies within 2 tiles: it ends on them, and they are immune to it for the rest of the fight.

mastered.name: Established Fact
mastered.flavour: You checked. It's true now.
mastered.text: Once per session, state a fact about the technology, biology or history in the scene. The Narrator makes it true, unless it contradicts something already shown. If the Narrator refuses the fact, you keep the use.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: Spend 2 AP to explain one visible enemy's weakness so simply that anyone can use it. Every ally within 6 tiles gets +2 to hit that enemy until your next turn starts.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

skills.name: Eloquence
skills.summary: Logic as a weapon.
skills.quiet: There is only one truth, and you happen to be holding it.
skills.notices: She said 'before the fire'; the fire was after. She's lying about when.

ep.speaker: Xander Badman of Monsieur Saul's Law Firm
quote: Fine, if you insist, I'll review all the evidence. Aaaand there's nothing worth reviewing. The dashcam at 11:45 shows, plain as day, the defendant stabbing a man to death. And I'm sick of your take-the-punch-take-the-bribe attitude, Your Honour, and your jury's too. The evidence is right there, so why no arrest? Because the defendant comes from a good family? Or because the pile of cash under the table is just too hard to pass up? You know what? As counsel for the plaintiff, I'm going to walk outside and tell the world I won. There is only one truth, and if you disagree it's because you're a pack of nitpicking self-servers. I WIN. BYE-BYE. CLOSE THE COURT.
ep.intro: Eloquence is your power to argue and debate logically, whether you're stuck in a battle of wits or a high courtroom. Believe in yourself, pick apart every word out of your opponent's mouth, cook up something clever and fire it back with confidence.
ep.effect: Persuading an enemy in a fight is harder to resist. Your Brief Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you must win EVERY conversation, and you'll use every trick there is, whether the other side meant harm or not. Good or bad? Depends.
ep.good: lawyers, preachers, politicians, keyboard warriors.
ep.bad: quiet types, people who hate arguing, people who'd rather argue with their fists.

perks.name: Overruled!
perks.t1: While an enemy carries a Left Brain Debuff you inflicted, you start your turn with 2 more AP. Once every 3 turns. While you carry one yourself, you start your turn with 2 AP less; that too happens at most once every 3 turns.
perks.t2: While an enemy carries a Left or Right Brain Debuff you inflicted, you start your turn with 2 more AP. Once every 3 turns. While you carry one yourself, you start your turn with 1 AP less; that too happens at most once every 3 turns.

perks.name: Burden of Proof
perks.t1: When someone accuses you or your squad, demand their evidence. If they can't produce it, they lose the argument outright. The Narrator decides whether they have any.
perks.t2: When someone accuses you or your squad, demand their evidence. If they can't produce it, they lose the argument outright and everyone watching shifts one step towards your side. The Narrator decides whether they have any.

mastered.name: Closing Argument
mastered.flavour: You didn't win the argument. You ended it.
mastered.text: Once per scene, make your closing argument. Every listener who isn't ruled by fear or faith accepts its logic, even if they hate where it leads, and an Eloquence check on the same point succeeds automatically. The Narrator decides what they do about it: they can still refuse to act.

combos.name: Just the Repairman
combos.text: While you carry a toolbox: when someone spots you sneaking, there is a 50% chance they take you for maintenance staff and you stay hidden from them. They don't look again that scene unless you attack.
combos.deed: Talk your way past a guard who caught you somewhere you shouldn't be.

combos.name: Spoon-Feed
combos.text: Spend 2 AP to explain one visible enemy's weakness so simply that anyone can use it. Every ally within 6 tiles gets +2 to hit that enemy until your next turn starts.
combos.deed: Teach someone a Sigil.

combos.name: Fire Sermon
combos.text: Spend 2 AP to preach; you can't while Silenced. Until your next turn starts, every Blessing you pray also forces each enemy within 4 tiles to make a Heart save or be Shaken.
combos.deed: Convert an enemy mid-fight.

skills.name: Visualization
skills.summary: Shapes thought into images and Sigils into forms.
skills.quiet: Thousand-autumn red. You'll never mix it. Try anyway.
skills.notices: The scorch marks fan out from the left. The blast came from the corner, not the door.

ep.speaker: Rémy Étienne, the Second Broom-Bearer
quote: Thinking it in your head is not enough! Master Sakamoto once spent four months mixing just 200 grams of watercolour. He called it 'Thousand-Autumn Red.' And if you must know: I've watched the video of him mixing it over a thousand times, and I still can't make that colour. No one can guess what you might do with a few rose stems, glue and an egg yolk. I wonder what 'Afternoon of Blood' looked like inside his mind. But the undeniable truth is that the way he carried that thought from his head onto paper is irresistible. A beauty only he could paint.
ep.intro: Visualization is your power to picture the world: to take the shapeless thoughts in your head and express them outward as images.
ep.effect: +5% elemental damage.
ep.high: you see the story behind every landscape and make landscapes out of every story. You risk sinking into faraway worlds and forgetting this one.
ep.good: critics, painters, Projector Gear® users.
ep.bad: the near-sighted, people who'd rather feel than describe.

perks.name: Mirage
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to project a false wall, figure or sound onto a tile in range; a new Mirage replaces the old one. Each enemy that sees or hears it rolls against your Visualization, and those that fail believe it until your next turn starts. A believer won't move or shoot through the wall, attacks the figure, or walks towards the sound.
perks.t2: Spend 2 AP to project two false walls, figures or sounds onto tiles in range; a new Mirage replaces the old ones. Each enemy that sees or hears one rolls against your Visualization, and those that fail believe it until the start of your turn after next. A believer won't move or shoot through a wall, attacks a figure, or walks towards a sound.

perks.name: Blueprint
perks.t1: Once per scene, outside a fight, sketch the ground ahead for your squad (on the area map it costs 1 action point). If a fight starts in that scene, you and every squadmate who saw the sketch have +1 Movement on your first turn.
perks.t2: Once per scene, outside a fight, sketch the ground ahead for your squad (on the area map it costs 1 action point). If a fight starts in that scene, you and every squadmate who saw the sketch have +2 Movement on your first turn.

mastered.name: Solid Image
mastered.flavour: If you imagine it hard enough, it has edges.
mastered.text: Once per fight, for 0 AP, make one of your Mirage projections real until your next turn starts. A wall blocks movement and sight for everyone. A figure takes the first hit aimed at you or one of your allies, then breaks.

combos.name: What Could Be
combos.text: Once per session, before a major decision, ask for a vision. The Narrator shows you the best outcome within reach, and one way to get there.
combos.deed: Talk someone out of a terrible choice by showing them where it leads.

skills.name: Improvisation
skills.summary: Making a thing work now with what is at hand. Fixes guns, gear and machines in the field, robot squadmates included.
skills.quiet: It doesn't have to be right. It has to hold.
skills.notices: That strap, that pipe and your belt. That's a splint.

ep.speaker: Drava Keel, salvage fitter of the Mandestra lowland yards
quote: The manual says a servo-hand wants a clean bench, a calibrated driver and four hours. I had a ditch, a soup spoon, and as long as it takes an Ork to cross a field. He still has the hand. Plans are lovely things. I have had hundreds, and every one of them died in the first minute, most of them louder than I did. What you have after that is whatever is in your pockets, and how fast you stop mourning the plan. The spoon is still in there, by the way. Load-bearing. Nobody tell him.
ep.intro: Improvisation is what you do when the plan is gone: making the thing in front of you work with whatever is at hand, right now, and working out why later.
ep.effect: −10% ambush damage taken. Field Repair restores more for each point from 3 up.
ep.high: nothing catches you flat and nothing stays broken near you. But you stop making plans at all, and the people who depend on you can never tell what you will do next.
ep.good: field mechanics, ditch medics, smugglers, anyone who performs for a living.
ep.bad: planners, quartermasters, whoever signed for the equipment.

perks.name: Jury-Rig
perks.t1: A broken weapon works one more time: use One more time to make a last shot or strike with it, at the weapon's usual AP. After that it stays broken until it is repaired.
perks.t2: A broken weapon works one more time: use One more time to make a last shot or strike with it, at the weapon's usual AP. After that it stays broken until it is repaired. Your Field Repair also restores twice as much on drones.

perks.name: Hot-Swap
perks.t1: Once per turn in a fight, drawing, putting away or swapping what your hands hold, or fitting a mod, costs 0 AP. A two-handed draw counts; armour doesn't.
perks.t2: Twice per turn in a fight, drawing, putting away or swapping what your hands hold, or fitting a mod, costs 0 AP. A two-handed draw counts; armour doesn't.

mastered.name: Overhaul
mastered.flavour: It left the factory good. It leaves your bench better.
mastered.text: Field Repair costs 1 AP and restores twice as much. After a long rest, you can give one weapon a permanent extra mod slot, once per weapon.

combos.name: Field Surgeon
combos.text: Your Field Repair works on a living ally next to you, for its usual AP and one spare-parts charge: it heals 3 HP per point of your Improvisation, raised by your Healing given and your level, and it gets a Downed ally back on their feet. Your heals on robotic allies work at full power.
combos.deed: Bring a squadmate back from below 10% HP.

skills.name: Charisma
skills.summary: Warmth, persuasion, and lying with a smile.
skills.quiet: A gentleman never passes up a conversation he's sure to win.
skills.notices: He wants to be asked, not ordered. Ask him about his ship; he loves it.

ep.speaker: Damian Nox, SuperUltraHyperExclusive Producer for Sibugar Entertainment
quote: I asked whether he'd like a glass of water or anything. Honestly, officers, that afternoon was the first time I'd met Mr. Duboi, and everything in my statement is true. Granted, keeping an electric chair in one's office isn't for everyone, but I'm a lover of the arts. I adore bold, satirical work; how could I not display one of the masterpieces of my collection? It was a regrettable accident. That chair was never used until Mr. Duboi volunteered himself into it. How was I to know he would switch the power on himself and die so needlessly? Tell the court I'll be there. A gentleman like me never passes up a conversation he is certain to win.
ep.intro: Charisma is the power of words: how well you persuade and steer a conversation, and how warm you come across while doing it. Extremely handy for lying and making things up.
ep.effect: An offer of terms is harder to refuse. Your Rally Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you can talk anyone into anything, but all that warmth makes some people see you as a spineless bootlicker. Depends who you're talking to.
ep.good: politicians, merchants, lawyers.
ep.bad: antiheroes, the antisocial, anyone who hates looking soft in a conversation.

perks.name: Talks Broke Down
perks.t1: When a fight breaks out of a talk your squad won, you have 2 more AP on your first turn, and again on every third turn after it. Once every 3 turns. When it breaks out of a talk your squad lost, you have 2 AP less on those turns instead. A fight breaks out of a talk when it starts in the same story round as your squad's last dialogue check, or the round after.
perks.t2: When a fight breaks out of a talk your squad won, you have 2 more AP on your first turn, and again on every third turn after it. Once every 3 turns. Whenever a fight breaks out of a talk, won or lost, the first enemy to act hesitates: it has 1 AP less in round 1. A fight breaks out of a talk when it starts in the same story round as your squad's last dialogue check, or the round after.

perks.name: Crowd Pleaser
perks.t1: When you talk to a crowd, you make one roll for the whole crowd, at +2. A crowd is 3 or more listeners within 8 tiles of you. In a fight, a Persuade or Threaten heard by 3 or more enemies is one roll against all of them, and their save is 2 harder.
perks.t2: When you talk to a crowd, you make one roll for the whole crowd, at +2, and you can turn the crowd against one person you name; the Narrator plays what the crowd does. A crowd is 3 or more listeners within 8 tiles of you. In a fight, a Persuade or Threaten heard by 3 or more enemies is one roll against all of them, and their save is 2 harder.

mastered.name: Everyone's Friend
mastered.flavour: You've known them for ten minutes. They'd lend you their car.
mastered.text: Once per scene, pick one person who doesn't already hate you. Until the scene ends they treat you as a trusted friend and share what a friend would; the Narrator plays them. Your first lie to them succeeds automatically.

combos.name: Make Way
combos.text: Moving past enemies never draws opportunity attacks from them; Overwatch can still fire. Crowds part for you: bystanders don't block your path, and the Narrator plays the rest.
combos.deed: Walk through a hostile crowd with no weapon drawn.

skills.name: Empathy
skills.summary: Feeling what the other side feels, enemies included.
skills.quiet: What was he thinking, right before? You'll wonder for years.
skills.notices: She isn't angry at you. She's terrified for the boy in the back.

ep.speaker: Paul Remarque
quote: I'd rather have been the one who took the bullet, you understand? Operation Daggerfall really did change the course of history. I know. I was there. What they praise and trumpet is partly true. But what they forgot? Too much.
I saw the eyes of a boy, sixteen or so, half burned black, lying still two metres above a pool of blood. What was he thinking before judgment day?

I saw the eyes of a father, half red, half black, fingers trembling as he cradled the body of a Crawler smaller than the rest. Right before Captain Kain called in another barrage. What was he thinking before those deafening blasts?

I saw. Horror... horror and pain, grief and helplessness. Oh, I'd give my whole fortune to forget, you understand? Forget the horror in their eyes, the horror I still feel in my chest, the horror no words can describe. The horror of an empty face hanging above an iron stake.
ep.intro: Empathy is the bridge between one person and another: feeling what someone else is going through, putting yourself where they stand, and understanding at least partly why they do what they do.
ep.effect: +10% healing given. From 3 points, one Pump of an Outburst each round is free. From 7 points, a held Outburst swells without Strain.
ep.high: you become one with humanity. You understand everyone's circumstances, and everyone's story gets into you. You cry other people's tears and stick your nose into business that isn't yours.
ep.good: therapists, human lie detectors, good alignments.
ep.bad: chaotic alignments, serial killers, non-humanoids.

perks.name: Shared Breath
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to link with an ally within 3 tiles that you can see. The next Heart debuff that lands on either of you lands on both, each for half its duration; then the link ends.
perks.t2: Spend 2 AP to link with an ally within 3 tiles that you can see, for the rest of the fight. Every Heart debuff that lands on either of you lands on both, each for half its duration.

perks.name: Lay Down Arms
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to plead with one humanoid enemy within 8 tiles who can hear you. It makes a Heart save or lowers its weapon: it can't attack on its next turn.
perks.t2: Spend 2 AP to plead with up to three humanoid enemies within 8 tiles who can hear you. Each makes a Heart save or lowers its weapon: it can't attack on its next turn.

mastered.name: Open Hand
mastered.flavour: You saw the moment they stopped wanting this. So did they.
mastered.text: When an enemy you can see drops to a quarter of its HP or less, you can offer it mercy for 0 AP, once per enemy. It makes a Heart save or surrenders for the rest of the fight. Bosses and machines never accept.

combos.name: Cold Read
combos.text: Whenever you Analyze someone, the Narrator also tells you privately what they want most.
combos.deed: Close a case with a confession.

skills.name: Camaraderie
skills.summary: The squad is a world of its own.
skills.quiet: You're not alone in this. You never were.
skills.notices: Kestrel hasn't eaten since the drop. Ask her, not the sergeant.

ep.speaker: Anastasia Vandenberg of Kemizuchi Military Academy
quote: If you don't want to get brainwashed, I'd stay away from that Souji. 'The power of friendship,' then 'the bond of hearts'; he says that stuff without a shred of embarrassment. He wants to befriend everyone he meets and goes around calling people 'comrade' before he's even graduated. Go into a fight with him and before you know it half the enemy team are on our side. Last week he talked that platinum-haired girl from the rival school onto our team, just like that. Is that insane or what? Jealous? Why on earth would I be jealous? Completely ridiculous!
ep.intro: Camaraderie is your teamwork and your solidarity with your squad, plus your knack for making friends and building factions.
ep.effect: +10% healing received.
ep.high: you become the heart of any team you join. You start seeing the team as its own little world and judge outsiders harder than you mean to.
ep.good: captains, team players.
ep.bad: lone wolves, edgelords, murder hobos.

perks.name: Soulmate
perks.t1: Outside a fight, bond with one teammate. You take part of the damage they take, in their place: 5% at Camaraderie Mastery 1, 10% at Mastery 2, 15% at Mastery 3 and 20% at Mastery 4. It never takes your last HP, and if they hold Soulmate too you do it for each other.
perks.t2: Outside a fight, bond with up to two teammates. You take part of the damage they take, in their place: 5% at Camaraderie Mastery 1, 10% at Mastery 2, 15% at Mastery 3 and 20% at Mastery 4. It never takes your last HP, and if they hold Soulmate too you do it for each other.

perks.name: Rally Cry
perks.t1: When an enemy or a hazard drops an ally to 0 HP, every other ally, you included, takes 15% less damage until their next turn starts.
perks.t2: When an enemy or a hazard drops an ally to 0 HP, every other ally, you included, takes 25% less damage until their next turn starts.

mastered.name: Many Hands
mastered.flavour: Nobody on this squad fights alone. Not even you.
mastered.text: Your Hand-Off reaches any ally within 3 tiles, not only one next to you. An ally you can see who has already used their reaction may use yours instead.

combos.name: Cultured
combos.text: You have +1 on Ingenuity and Charisma checks whenever the talk turns to art, history or holo-dramas: you blend in with anyone who loves them. The Narrator decides when that applies.
combos.deed: Win someone over with a story, a song or a painting.

combos.name: Field Surgeon
combos.text: Your Field Repair works on a living ally next to you, for its usual AP and one spare-parts charge: it heals 3 HP per point of your Improvisation, raised by your Healing given and your level, and it gets a Downed ally back on their feet. Your heals on robotic allies work at full power.
combos.deed: Bring a squadmate back from below 10% HP.

combos.name: Silent Partner
combos.text: When you hide, one ally next to you becomes Hidden with you. They lose it when they end a move away from you, or when you are found.
combos.deed: Get the whole squad through a guarded area unseen.

skills.name: Insinuation
skills.summary: Metaphor, subtext, poetry and flirting.
skills.quiet: The perfume of corpse-flowers. Someone in this room is rotting.
skills.notices: 'The river was high' means the shipment came early. She's telling you without telling them.

ep.speaker: Aleksandr Donovik Artem of Rigaz Trade Company ADCorp
quote: Jazmine, Jazmine of the dying afternoon, lead the lost soul away from breaking.

Ask ten people in the recon squad and nine won't want to share a transport with me. They say the way I talk isn't easy on the ears. I can rarely sit with someone ten minutes before something about them grates on me, and saying it plainly would be a little... vulgar. So I use metaphor. A faint sweat stain becomes 'the perfume of corpse-flowers in the Sonz marsh.' An uncleaned rifle becomes 'a homemade death at dawn.' I won't hide it: watching them fume without a comeback always brightens my heart a little.

I've lived alone between earth and sky too long for one or two more haters to matter. But Jazmine is something else. Coarse as an old man from Chezknov, and yet sometimes... gentle as a golden lotus in a stinking marsh. Can your smile melt my heart? Hard to say. The one thing I know for certain: you make me want to be a better man.
ep.intro: Implication is your command of metaphor. You catch people's meaning when they talk in figures, you understand difficult poetry and literature, and it helps a great deal with lying and with flirting. (With literature. It can't generate a credit card.)
ep.effect: Your Taunt Call reaches 1 tile further and is harder to shake off. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you drown in the meaning behind every word. Every metaphor lands, but you fall into the "yes means no, no means yes" trap.
ep.good: poets, writers, artists, the hopelessly lovestruck.
ep.bad: the antisocial, blunt people, paladins.

perks.name: Sweet Talker
perks.t1: Charm or flatter someone with a successful Charisma or Insinuation check. For the rest of that scene, putting a buff or a debuff on them gives you 2 AP. Once every 3 turns. If someone you charmed puts a debuff on you, you have 2 AP less on your next turn: betrayal stings. That too happens at most once every 3 turns.
perks.t2: Charm or flatter someone with a successful Charisma or Insinuation check. For the rest of that scene, putting a buff or a debuff on them gives you 3 AP. Once every 3 turns.

perks.name: Double Meaning
perks.t1: Say one sentence that means one thing to the enemy and another to your squad. The squad gets +2 on the action you hinted at; the Narrator decides which roll that is. In a fight, once per round and for 0 AP, name an enemy within 8 tiles: each squad member's next attack on it gets +2 until your next turn.
perks.t2: Say one sentence that means one thing to the enemy and another to your squad. The squad gets +2 on the action you hinted at, and the enemy acts on the false meaning; the Narrator plays both. In a fight, once per round and for 0 AP, name an enemy within 8 tiles: each squad member's next attack on it gets +2 until your next turn, and the nearest other enemy that heard you loses 2 AP on its next turn.

mastered.name: Their Own Idea
mastered.flavour: You never told them. You just let them get there.
mastered.text: Once per scene, hide a suggestion inside a sentence. The listener believes it was their own idea and acts on it; the Narrator plays how. It fails if it would harm them directly, and an important or supernatural listener gets a Heart save against your Insinuation.

combos.name: Verse of War
combos.text: Speak a line of verse, then Begin or Release an Outburst with In verse on: it gets +1 tile of range and +10% damage.
combos.deed: Cast an Outburst that ends a fight, and say something worth remembering while you do it.

skills.name: Will Power
skills.summary: The strength of the soul, and of its link to its twin in the upper realm. Attack skill for Soul spells that strike.
skills.quiet: Breathe deep. Meditate until the doubt falls away.
skills.notices: The air here is thick. The heart can draw deep, but slowly.

ep.speaker: Nora the "Witch" of Arkvelton
quote: Yes, your heart can shatter like silken tofu. Connecting to the twin world is no joke. Pulling a few little sparks over ten minutes, anyone with a cheap Emanator can do that. A bolt over ten thousand volts in two seconds? Try it and you'll learn what a Mana Short is. There was a Linker once who didn't just bleed internally; he shorted so hard his heart burst on the spot and left a hole in his chest. Outburst craft needs a pure heart, the strength to resist temptation, and the understanding to hold the connection. Now breathe deep and meditate until your doubts fall away!
ep.intro: Will Power is the strength of your heart: generosity and spiritual sharpness. A person's soul lives in the heart, and Will Power measures both your mental strength and the strength of the soul inside you. Essential for Outbursts and Emanators.
ep.effect: +10% Soul power. +10% mana syphoned. Every 2 points: +1 Strain limit, Outbursts reach 1 tile further, and you keep 1 more design ready. Every 3 points: 1 more module slot. Your Outbursts' conditions are harder to save against.
ep.high: your heart and soul turn hard and strong. You connect easily with the supernatural, but you slip easily into delusion, because the link to your upper-realm soul is so strong you can't tell this world from that one.
ep.good: Emanator users, monks, crusaders, Bonders.
ep.bad: Evoker users, scientists, melee users.

perks.name: Heart Overload
perks.t1: Once a turn, right after you Release an Outburst at stage 2 or higher, you can Begin the same design again at once for 0 AP. You pay its mana and Strain as usual, and it holds at stage 0. If you don't have the mana for that Begin, you can pay it in HP instead, at 1 HP per point of mana, but an Outburst paid for in blood can't heal or shield. You need an Emanator in hand.
perks.t2: Once a turn, right after you Release an Outburst at stage 2 or higher, you can Begin the same design again at once for 0 AP. You pay its mana and Strain as usual, and it holds at stage 1 if you have not taken your free Pump this turn (at stage 0 if you have). If you don't have the mana for that Begin, you can pay it in HP instead, at 1 HP per point of mana, but an Outburst paid for in blood can't heal or shield. You need an Emanator in hand.

perks.name: Resonance
perks.t1: Each Outburst you Release gives your next Release in this fight +10% to its effect, building up to +20%. You lose what you have built when you end a turn in which you neither held nor Released an Outburst. This adds to the bonus you get when allies Release in the same round.
perks.t2: Each Outburst you Release gives your next Release in this fight +10% to its effect, building up to +30%. An ally's Release that you can see adds a step too. You lose what you have built when you end a turn in which you neither held nor Released an Outburst. This adds to the bonus you get when allies Release in the same round.

mastered.name: The Twin Pays
mastered.flavour: Up there, someone with your face flinches. Down here, the spell lands.
mastered.text: Once per fight, when you Begin an Outburst, choose The Twin Pays: the Begin costs no AP, no mana and no Strain, and holding it costs no Strain. Your twin in the upper realm pays for it.

combos.name: Verse of War
combos.text: Speak a line of verse, then Begin or Release an Outburst with In verse on: it gets +1 tile of range and +10% damage.
combos.deed: Cast an Outburst that ends a fight, and say something worth remembering while you do it.

combos.name: Twin Souls
combos.text: Once per session, outside a fight, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question; the Narrator answers truthfully. Your Outbursts can also carry a third school, as a rider at half strength, for 20 more MP.
combos.deed: Survive a Mana Short.

skills.name: Composure
skills.summary: A face that never moves.
skills.quiet: Stand still. Then stand stiller.
skills.notices: His eyes slipped off yours. That was the moment. He's done.

ep.speaker: Kaizer Meyer Reinch Wolf of Central Command Center
quote: In the ring, kid, the first punch you throw doesn't come from your fist. What you need is your eyes! When he walks at you, arms up and chest out, you stand still. When your lips feel his boozy breath, you stand still. When his bloodthirsty stare locks on yours, you stand stiller. Only when his eyes slip off yours do you get to move. The only problem is, the fight ended long before that.
ep.intro: Composure is your ability to stay calm in any situation. Neither a monster at midnight nor the woman waiting at the end of the alley can move your face an inch.
ep.effect: +1 on Heart saves (fear, despair, losing your nerve).
ep.high: your face goes stone in every situation. Great when someone threatens or interrogates you; terrible for anyone who just wants to be friendly.
ep.good: security guards, police, iron men, lead men.
ep.bad: small bois, shy bois, studs and sluts.

perks.name: You Get Used to It
perks.t1: The first time each round an ally within 5 tiles takes a Brain or Heart condition, your next save this round is at +2: you have seen worse.
perks.t2: The first time each round an ally within 5 tiles takes a Brain or Heart condition, your next save this round is at +4: you have seen worse. You may give that bonus to the ally instead, for their next save this round; it costs you nothing.

perks.name: Flat Line
perks.t1: When a fight starts, your calm unnerves the most dangerous enemy: it has −1 to its attacks while it can see you and you are standing. Until the end of your first turn you may move this to another enemy for 0 AP.
perks.t2: When a fight starts, your calm unnerves the most dangerous enemy: it has −2 to its attacks while it can see you and you are standing. Until the end of your first turn you may move this to another enemy for 0 AP.

mastered.name: Still Water
mastered.flavour: Nothing goes in. Nothing comes out.
mastered.text: You are immune to Brain debuffs. Enemies can't read you: not your intent, your lies or your HP, not even with Analyze or Empathy. Your allies still can.

combos.name: Between Heartbeats
combos.text: Once per fight, when an enemy you can see starts an action, you act first with 2 free AP: a shot at it, a move, dropping Prone, a stim for an ally next to you, or a reload. You choose which on your turn, and it waits until an enemy sets it off. It doesn't use your reaction.
combos.deed: Come through an ambush without being hit.

combos.name: The Voice
combos.text: Once per session, in a fight, give an order for 0 AP. Every rank-and-file enemy within 8 tiles makes a Heart save or obeys it on its next turn: halt, hold fire, drop its weapon, kneel or fall back. Elites and bosses ignore it, and the Narrator decides what any other order does.
combos.deed: Stare down an enemy officer until they back off.

skills.name: Lore Master
skills.summary: The occultist's library: old scripts, curses, relics and the names of things.
skills.quiet: Mother wanted to know. So do you.
skills.notices: That mark is a Lumeri saint's seal, but upside down. It's a warning, not a blessing.

ep.speaker: Andrade Lovelace, "Mother" of the Institute of Forgotten Knowledge
quote: Mother lived to hear every story from a thousand worlds. It was a small dream from when I was young and foolish, a spark struck the moment I walked into the modest little library my father kept in secret. It grew into a roaring fire in my heart: a hunger to touch every stream of knowledge that science calls baseless. The marches of the half-horse Zarkast tribe. Tales of wicked witches in the woods outside Albert Town. Rumours of magic gates that transform those who pass. Love stories between humans and beings of the upper realm.
Mother wanted to know, to understand, to hold the chance to prove it true. And after more than a hundred years of study, they chose Mother for this seat. The one who makes the unreal real.
ep.intro: Lore Master is how well you adapt to and absorb supernatural knowledge, the kind science dismisses as baseless. You understand how it works without leaning on dangerous shortcuts like charms or spiritual links.
ep.effect: Your Name It Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: you can tell at once whether something is the work of the supernatural and how to deal with it. Comfortable among mages, but you start rejecting proven science because you see the supernatural threads behind it.
ep.good: dreamers, divine casters, spellswords.
ep.bad: scientists, hackers, barbarians.

perks.name: Old Tongue
perks.t1: You can read any ancient or upper-realm script. The Narrator tells you what it says.
perks.t2: You can read and speak any ancient or upper-realm script. Once per being, an upper-realm being you speak to will parley with you; in a fight it holds its attacks on its next turn while it listens, though it may still move. The Narrator plays the parley.

perks.name: Rite in the Field
perks.t1: In a fight, wards and rituals cost you 1 AP less: drawing a WARD glyph, beginning an Outburst that makes allies Guarded, a Ward class move, praying and Crystallise. None of them drops below 1 AP (half an AP for the glyph).
perks.t2: In a fight, wards and rituals cost you 2 AP less: drawing a WARD glyph, beginning an Outburst that makes allies Guarded, a Ward class move, praying and Crystallise. None of them drops below 1 AP (half an AP for the glyph).

mastered.name: True Name
mastered.flavour: You know what it's called. It knows you know.
mastered.text: Once per session, for 0 AP, speak the true name of an upper-realm being, a cursed thing or a creature. It must have been Analyzed first. For the rest of the scene it takes 50% more damage from you and your allies, and it can't lie to you; the Narrator plays that.

combos.name: Cultured
combos.text: You have +1 on Ingenuity and Charisma checks whenever the talk turns to art, history or holo-dramas: you blend in with anyone who loves them. The Narrator decides when that applies.
combos.deed: Win someone over with a story, a song or a painting.

combos.name: Twin Souls
combos.text: Once per session, outside a fight, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question; the Narrator answers truthfully. Your Outbursts can also carry a third school, as a rider at half strength, for 20 more MP.
combos.deed: Survive a Mana Short.

skills.name: Faith
skills.summary: The saints judge. You deliver.
skills.quiet: Only the saints may judge. You only deliver.
skills.notices: The pilgrims keep the left aisle clear. Someone important is coming.

ep.speaker: Sister October of the Lumeri Church
quote: Holy Father Nerukhan taught that the love between people is everlasting. The world above where He reigns is no different from the world of men. But as a keeper of the saint's faith, I cannot sit idle before their contemptible deeds one more day.
Only the saints may judge and carry out justice. But delivering the sinners into their hands? That is our job.
*racks shotgun*
*heavy metal plays*
ep.intro: Faith is your ability to place your trust in higher powers. In a world where anything can happen, plenty of people face life's cruelty on the strength of belief. And unlike real life, here the odds of a prayer coming true are better than 1%.
ep.effect: +10% Blessing power. Hymns come back sooner: each point takes three quarters of a round off the wait, down to 3 rounds. Your Blessings' conditions are harder to save against.
ep.high: your bond with your faith tightens and amplifies everything your religion gives you. Everyone else sees an insufferable zealot, or worse, a heretic.
ep.good: crusaders, divine classes, cultists, missionaries.
ep.bad: atheists, scientists, smartasses.

perks.name: Litany
perks.t1: Spend 2 AP to speak a prayer: you and allies within 3 tiles get +1 on all saves until your next turn starts. You can't speak it while Silenced, and two Litanies don't add up.
perks.t2: Spend 2 AP to speak a prayer: you and allies within 3 tiles get +2 on all saves until your next turn starts. You can't speak it while Silenced, and two Litanies don't add up.

perks.name: Holy Ordnance
perks.t1: Spend 3 AP to bless the magazine in your own gun or in the gun of an ally next to you. Its rounds deal +20% damage to upper-realm and cursed beings until that magazine is swapped out.
perks.t2: Spend 3 AP to bless the magazine in your own gun or in the gun of an ally next to you, and the next one loaded after it. Their rounds deal +40% damage to upper-realm and cursed beings until each magazine is swapped out.

mastered.name: Judgement Day
mastered.flavour: The saints have looked. They've decided.
mastered.text: Once per fight, spend 3 AP to judge one enemy you can see. Its next attack against you or an ally fails automatically, and your attacks deal 50% more damage to it until the fight ends.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 3 AP · Once per combat

combos.name: Fire Sermon
combos.text: Spend 2 AP to preach; you can't while Silenced. Until your next turn starts, every Blessing you pray also forces each enemy within 4 tiles to make a Heart save or be Shaken.
combos.deed: Convert an enemy mid-fight.

skills.name: Conscience
skills.summary: Seeing where an act leads.
skills.quiet: It is not a question of right or left. Only of conscience.
skills.notices: If you take the platinum, the robots stay behind. That is the whole of the choice.

ep.speaker: The Azure Blood Holder
quote: It is not a question of right or wrong. Nor of left or right. In a world of upheaval and chaos, the only thing that makes a God or a Demon is conscience.
ep.intro: Conscience is your ability to tell right from wrong, and to see the good or harm in an act not just now but far into the future, not just for you but for all of humanity.
ep.effect: +10% to every shield you are given.
ep.high: you understand the consequences of everything you're about to do. But you think from one angle only, good or evil, right or wrong, and yours is the only one that counts.
ep.good: lawful alignments, living saints, Satan in human skin.
ep.bad: neutral alignments, emotionless robots, weathervanes.

perks.name: Red Line
perks.t1: Outside a fight, name one line you won't cross. While you hold to it, you have +1 on every Heart save. The Narrator decides when you cross it; after that you can't name a new line until the next session.
perks.t2: Outside a fight, name one line you won't cross. While you hold to it, you have +2 on every Heart save and allies within 3 tiles have +1. The Narrator decides when you cross it; after that you can't name a new line until the next session.

perks.name: Clean Hands
perks.t1: Once per turn, when you spare an enemy or protect an innocent, you gain a shield worth 15% of your max HP. To spare an enemy, attack with Spare on: a blow that would take its last HP subdues it instead. Outside a fight, the Narrator decides what counts.
