perks.t2: Once per turn, when you spare an enemy or protect an innocent, you gain a shield worth 25% of your max HP. To spare an enemy, attack with Spare on: a blow that would take its last HP subdues it instead. Outside a fight, the Narrator decides what counts.

mastered.name: Foreseen
mastered.flavour: You saw where it led. This time you take the other road.
mastered.text: Once per session, after a major decision goes wrong, rewind to just before it. Everyone at the table has to agree. Everything since is undone, the Narrator tells you what would have happened, and you choose again.

combos.name: What Could Be
combos.text: Once per session, before a major decision, ask for a vision. The Narrator shows you the best outcome within reach, and one way to get there.
combos.deed: Talk someone out of a terrible choice by showing them where it leads.

skills.name: Authority
skills.summary: The measure of cool, and your Leadership rating.
skills.quiet: They'll fall in line. They always do.
skills.notices: The guards are watching you, not him. You could just tell them to stand aside.

ep.speaker: Brengan Springfield, the "Juggernaut" of the 101st Hellraiser Division
quote: I don't need to tell you about Hank Ladan's war record, kid. Everything you need, you'll get from watching how people treat him.

A skinny frame in a plain, no-frills uniform. Easy stance, warm laugh. Nobody would guess Hank Ladan outranks a marshal, and nobody dares look him in the eye, or at the five stars on his shoulder. Not even a guy like me who won three straight wrestling tournaments in the Marine mess hall. Something comes off him that makes your knees want to buckle, out of respect or fear. He has the nepo babies over in the Air branch falling in line, and every agent in the enforcement bureau bows when he passes. A busted-up marine like me? Honestly, I'd rather hunt ten Ork fangs in one afternoon than hear one word of criticism from him.
ep.intro: Authority is the measure of cool. Anyone can put on a suit; Authority decides whether you look cool in it. Be the groomsman and still draw more of the bride's eyes and respect than the groom. Oh, so dignified.
ep.effect: Karma moves 1 further each time it changes: more when it is awarded, more when it is taken. Your Order Call reaches 1 tile further. On a check it rolls 1 better than its points say.
ep.high: people mistake you for a general, a leader or a top CEO, which raises the odds you get investigated and make the news for buying apples at the market instead of the supermarket.
ep.good: soldiers, police, security, teachers, anyone who has to be cool.
ep.bad: sugar babies, fuckboys (you risk ending up married instead of a one-night stand).

perks.name: Outclassed
perks.t1: If your squad makes the first kill of a fight and you had damaged that enemy, you have 3 more AP on your next turn. If your squad takes the fight's first casualty, you have 2 AP less on your next turn.
perks.t2: If your squad makes the first kill of a fight and you had damaged that enemy, you have 3 more AP on your next turn, and whoever made the kill has 1 more AP on theirs.

perks.name: Real Power
perks.t1: Once per organisation, ask who really holds the power in it, whatever the titles say. The Narrator tells you.
perks.t2: Once per organisation, ask who really holds the power in it, whatever the titles say. The Narrator tells you, and that person agrees to see you; what they agree to after that is up to them.

mastered.name: On My Mark
mastered.flavour: You say go. They're already gone.
mastered.text: Once per round, on your turn, spend 1 AP to order an ally who can hear you. They take one action at once, outside their turn, with up to 4 AP. The AP they spend comes off their next turn.
mastered.meta: Active skill · 1 AP · Once per round

combos.name: The Voice
combos.text: Once per session, in a fight, give an order for 0 AP. Every rank-and-file enemy within 8 tiles makes a Heart save or obeys it on its next turn: halt, hold fire, drop its weapon, kneel or fall back. Elites and bosses ignore it, and the Narrator decides what any other order does.
combos.deed: Stare down an enemy officer until they back off.

attrs.name: Intelligence
attrs.fx: Sigil words per spell and Sigil damage

attrs.name: Expression
attrs.fx: Sigil AP cost and elemental damage

attrs.name: Insight
attrs.fx: Healing given, Soul spell cost and some Max MP

attrs.fx: Soul damage, Max MP and Mana Syphon

classesFull.name: Bulwark
classesFull.moveText: Costs 2 AP. You gain Guard equal to your Durability points (at least 1; you hold 5 at most) and become Braced: +2 Defense until you move, are pushed or are knocked Prone. While you hold Guard you Interpose: when an enemy's weapon attack hits an ally next to you, you spend 1 Guard and your reaction and take the hit yourself, with your own armour. A fight starts with 1 Guard for you (the Bulwark's).

classesFull.name: Breaker
classesFull.moveText: Costs the AP of your melee attack and 1 Momentum. Move up to 2 tiles and strike an enemy, all in one action. The move provokes no opportunity attacks. Once a turn, your first hit on a Shaken or Frightened enemy, with any weapon, gives you 1 Momentum (the Breaker's).

classesFull.name: Skirmisher
classesFull.moveText: Your Aimed attacks have +1 to hit, and with a weapon that has Heat they add none. Once a turn, on your turn, a weapon technique that costs 3 AP or more costs 1 AP less (a Burst, a Mag Dump, a dear blow: any weapon). The attacks everyone has (a shot, an Aimed shot, a blow) are never cheaper.

classesFull.name: Operative
classesFull.moveText: Costs 1 AP. An enemy you can see becomes Marked until the fight ends: your squad gets +1 to hit it, and it can't become Hidden. You can keep 3 enemies Marked; a fourth Mark lifts the oldest one.

classesFull.name: Sigilist
classesFull.moveText: The damage words FIRE, FREEZE, SHOCK, STONE and ACID cost 1 charge less to draw: 1 instead of 2. SPARK and GALE already cost the least a glyph can and stay there, because no glyph costs less than 1 charge.

classesFull.name: Rigger
classesFull.moveText: Analyze costs you 1 AP, and it also shows what the target means to do on its next turn.

classesFull.name: Mender
classesFull.moveText: Costs 2 AP. Heal an ally next to you for 5 × your Healing given, more as you level, and end their Bleeding. It uses no Supplies, and works once per ally per turn. Out of a fight you have time to work: three times as much, once per ally per scene. You can also Stabilise a Downed ally next to you for 1 AP: they come back at 1 HP, with no stim needed.

classesFull.name: Channeler
classesFull.moveText: While you hold a Damage Outburst, you get your one free Pump a turn even without Empathy 3. And your free Pump each turn, wherever it comes from, adds +0.1 more to the multiplier.

classesFull.name: Chaplain
classesFull.moveText: A Buff-school cast: it costs your Soul cast AP and 20 MP (before the ambient mana is counted), and adds Strain like any cast. You, or an ally you can see within Soul reach, gains a shield of 12 × your Healing given until the fight ends. It grows with your level, like healing. If they already have a bigger shield, that one stays.

families.name: Frontline
families.blurb: Hold the line, or break theirs.

families.name: Guns and hunters
families.blurb: Range, patience and a lot of brass.

families.name: Sigil casters
families.blurb: Mind magic: command words drawn through an Evoker.

families.name: Soul and faith
families.blurb: Heart magic, prayer and the things that answer.

families.name: Voices and leaders
families.blurb: Words as weapons, people as armies.

families.name: Hybrids and wanderers
families.blurb: Two trades at once, or a little of everything.

families.name: All-in
families.blurb: Everything in one place: one attribute at 7, its skill at 7, and almost nothing else. A 7/1/1 character.

items.name: Holdfast
items.blurb: Stands in the doorway so nobody else has to. Has been shot more times than most people have been hugged.

items.name: Bodyguard
items.blurb: Sees the knife before the client does, and gets between them. Paid by the day, loyal past it.

items.name: Brawler
items.blurb: Fixes problems with fists and leaves the paperwork to people with smaller hands.

items.name: Berserker
items.blurb: Doesn't feel the wound until the fight is over, and doesn't stop until somebody makes it over.

items.name: Fencer
items.blurb: Blade or pistol, the same rule: be somewhere else when they swing.

items.name: Monk
items.blurb: Trained until the body and the breath became one weapon. Calm right up to the point of impact.

items.name: Sharpshooter
items.blurb: Identify. Squeeze. Breathe. Patient as stone, and the last thing a lot of people never saw.

items.name: Heavy Gunner
items.blurb: Carries the gun nobody else can lift and believes volume of fire is a personality.

items.name: Ranger
items.blurb: Reads tracks, wind and silence. Knows where the enemy is before the map does.

items.name: Grenadier
items.blurb: Every problem is a load-bearing wall, and every wall has a weak spot.

items.name: Intruder
items.blurb: In and out before the guard finishes yawning. Nobody remembers seeing them, which is the point.

items.name: Stalker
items.blurb: Waits in the dark for the right moment, then becomes the reason people fear the dark.

items.name: Thief
items.blurb: Light fingers, quick hands, and a professional respect for good locks.

items.name: Spy
items.blurb: Smiles, lies and never sweats. Has had four names this year and liked two of them.

items.name: Glyphwright
items.blurb: Draws FIRE · SEEK · SPREAD faster than most people draw breath. Smells faintly of scorched Evoker.

items.name: Sentinel
items.blurb: Raises walls of command words around the squad, and lectures them about it afterwards.

items.name: Enchanter
items.blurb: Inscribes the squad's gear before the fight, so the fight is shorter than it should be.

items.name: Jinx
items.blurb: Finds the weakness, names it, and makes it worse. Enemies blind, slow and confused, in that order.

items.name: Detective
items.blurb: First: no casings. Second: the wall is dented from the far side. Third: you're lying.

items.name: Engineer
items.blurb: Keeps the guns firing, the doors opening and the robots alive. Talks to machines more than people.

items.name: Scholar
items.blurb: Has read about it. Has read about everything. Will tell you, at length, in the middle of the firefight.

items.name: Stormcaller
items.blurb: Imagines the lightning so hard the world gives it to them. Heart pounding, hands smoking.

items.name: Empath
items.blurb: Feels your wound from across the room and closes it before you finish screaming.

items.name: Confessor
items.blurb: Hears the squad's sins, prays over their wounds, and reports to nobody but the saints.

items.name: Zealot
items.blurb: Only the saints may judge. The zealot delivers. Usually with a shotgun.

items.name: Witch
items.blurb: Knows the old stories are true and the twin world is listening. Respected, feared, never invited twice.

items.name: Harbinger
items.blurb: Speaks in omens. Enemies hear their own worst fear in every word, and run from it.

items.name: Silver Tongue
items.blurb: Can talk anyone into anything, and has talked several people into regretting it.

items.name: Troubadour
items.blurb: Turns a squad into a chorus. Morale goes up, enemy morale goes elsewhere.

items.name: Captain
items.blurb: Doesn't raise their voice. Doesn't need to. People simply do what they say.

items.name: Enforcer
items.blurb: Every conversation ends with the other side agreeing. How it gets there is up to them.

items.name: Spellblade
items.blurb: Draws Sigils with the sword tip. Three slashes, then a storm opens in the enemy's head.

items.name: Crusader
items.blurb: Strong arm, certain heart. Walks into the dark first and says a word for those who don't walk out.

items.name: Witch Hunter
items.blurb: Knows what the shadow is, and what kind of round it needs.

items.name: Field Medic
items.blurb: Under fire, on their knees, hands in someone's chest, telling them a terrible joke. Never leaves anyone behind.

items.name: Survivor
items.blurb: Lived where nothing lives. Throws first, ducks second, eats whatever's left.

items.name: Drifter
items.blurb: A little of everything and no home in any of it. Never quite who the room expects.

items.name: Living Wall
items.blurb: Doesn't dodge. Doesn't need to.

items.name: Wrecking Ball
items.blurb: One swing settles the argument, and the wall behind it.

items.name: Deadeye
items.blurb: Never the second shot.

items.name: Phantom
items.blurb: Was in the room the whole time. Nobody remembers letting them in.

items.name: Savant
items.blurb: Draws a Sigil before the rest of the room finishes the word.

items.name: Illusionist
items.blurb: Pictures the fire so clearly the Evoker can't tell it's not there yet.

items.name: Heartreader
items.blurb: Hears what you meant, not what you said, and answers that.

items.name: Unbroken
items.blurb: The heart holds. Everything in front of it doesn't.

items.name: Prophet
items.blurb: Their patron answers on the first ring.

origins.name: Central City
origins.Home: Earth, the capital of the old centre.
origins.Upbringing: precincts, bank cards, shock batons, somebody else doing the dirty work.
origins.You know: city services, officials, the precincts, the inner ring's gossip, how to get anything done with paperwork.
origins.People see you as: soft, rich, connected, out of place past the walls.
origins.Traits that fit: Central City Kid, Inner Ring Heir, Slicer, Wanted, Machine-Faced, Right of Way.
origins.Hook: a family account someone at the CCEC is watching.

origins.name: The Thousand-Planet frontier
origins.Home: an extraction world, outpost or mining moon of the Thousand-Planet City.
origins.Upbringing: quotas, shift sirens, robots doing the jobs nobody survives.
origins.You know: mining, logistics, outpost life, the Thousand World Legion's ranks and rackets.
origins.People see you as: hard-working, expendable, owned by the quota.
origins.Traits that fit: Glass Runner, Heavyworlder, Symbol of Order, Field Medic, Moon Hunter.
origins.Hook: the foreman who still owes you a shift's pay.

origins.name: Hellraiser camps
origins.Home: the barracks worlds and mess halls behind the Hellraiser front.
origins.Upbringing: a soldier's child, or a soldier from sixteen. Orks were the bedtime story, and then the job.
origins.You know: Hellraiser doctrine, Orks, weapons, field rations, which officers get people killed.
origins.People see you as: brave, loud, disposable, a thug to the polite.
origins.Traits that fit: Forlorn Hope, Spray and Pray, Grenadier's Arm, Live to Fight Another Day, Squad Anchor.
origins.Hook: a sergeant who'd take you back, and a deserter who wants you to say nothing.

origins.name: Lumeri cloisters
origins.Home: a cloister or pilgrim world of the Lumeri Church.
origins.Upbringing: rites, scripture, the saints' feast days, nuns who could field-strip a shotgun.
origins.You know: the Church, its saints and Holy Father Nerukhan, its rites, its politics, its charity.
origins.People see you as: devout, trustworthy, judgemental, the Church's eyes.
origins.Traits that fit: Mind Without Fog, True Believer, Heretic, Pacifist.
origins.Hook: the abbess who expects a report.

origins.name: The Adamantile Brigade
origins.Home: a fortress-house of the knightly order.
origins.Upbringing: squire to a knight who slept in snake pits and arm-wrestled concrete for fun.
origins.You know: the Brigade's oaths and feuds, heavy arms, endurance, the Church's ceremonies.
origins.Traits that fit: Sworn Sibling, Pain Eater, Squad Anchor.
origins.Hook: the knight you squired for, still alive, still asking for help with breakfast.

origins.name: Kemizuchi, or the school across town
origins.Home: the officer academy, or its rival.
origins.Upbringing: drills, rankings, rivalries, friendship speeches nobody was embarrassed by.
origins.You know: officers, tactics, the old-boy network, the rival school's secrets (or yours).
origins.Traits that fit: Blade Recluse, Drill Echo, Rival, Born Officer.
origins.Hook: your classmate, now outranking you. (Suggested: the rival school quietly takes mixed families' children.)

origins.name: Arkvelton
origins.Upbringing: breathing exercises, meditation, the heart's link to the twin world, friends who shorted out.
origins.You know: Soul magic, Emanators, Mana Shorts, witch lore, the stories outside Albert Town.
origins.People see you as: a witch, gifted, dangerous, faintly heretical.
origins.Hook: the teacher who told you never to come back without the thing you took.

origins.name: The southern sects
origins.Home: the martial sects of the south.
origins.Upbringing: forms, katas and Sigils drawn with fists and blades. Professor Avdol sneers at people like you.
origins.You know: martial arts, the sects' lineages and feuds, Blade Scribe lore.
origins.Hook: a sect elder who wants a scroll back.

origins.name: The scholar halls
origins.Home: the Science Team's labs, a university, or the Institute of Forgotten Knowledge.
origins.Upbringing: libraries, lectures, Evokers, or banned books.
origins.You know: Sigil theory, history, science (or the occult), who's publishing what.
origins.People see you as: clever, useless in a fight, insufferable.
origins.Traits that fit: Sigil Savant, Occultist, Bottle Butts for Eyes, Cold Case.
origins.Hook: a research partner who credited themselves for your work.

origins.name: Mandestra and the trade lanes
origins.Home: a merchant house, a market stall, or a Rigaz Trade Company posting.
origins.Upbringing: haggling, ledgers, armed caravans, contracts with small print.
origins.You know: prices, routes, merchants, the RTC, who's smuggling what.
origins.Traits that fit: Market Blood, Company Man, Cover Story, Lunarshine.
origins.Hook: a creditor, and a shipment that never arrived.

origins.name: The gold-coin frontier
origins.Home: a frontier town past Central City's reach, where gold coins are money and the Smetanita Conjunction is the law.
origins.Upbringing: saloons, debts, favours, the Papa's people on every corner.
origins.You know: the black market, crime families, smuggling, frontier law.
origins.Traits that fit: Gambler, Wanted, Cover Story, Rogue Element.
origins.Hook: a favour you owe the Conjunction.

origins.name: The lowlands
origins.Home: Earth's ruined lowlands past the desert: Black Scavenger country, a forest of dead buildings.
origins.You know: ruins, scavenging, traps, survival, the Black Scavengers.
origins.Hook: the scavenger crew that thinks you're dead.

origins.name: Bazaim
origins.Home: the human nation that made peace with Daggerfall's survivors.
origins.Upbringing: neighbours with abilities, families mixed by love, Central City's spies everywhere.
origins.You know: espers, the truth about Crawlers (you've seen them as people), Bazaim's politics, how the CCEC operates.
origins.People see you as (in Central City): a spy, a traitor, a monster-lover.
origins.Traits that fit: Crawler-Blooded (needs a review against the one-way curse), Cover Story, Heaven's Faithful.
origins.Hook: someone in your family is a Crawler, and you can see them.

origins.name: The Ork borderlands
origins.Home: the frontier where human towns sit next to Ork warbands.
origins.Upbringing: raids, truces, trading with the enemy, maybe raised by them.
origins.You know: Orks, their warbands and parley, border survival.
origins.People see you as: half-savage, a traitor to some, a guide to others.
origins.Traits that fit: Raised by Orks, Beast Handler, Moon Hunter.
origins.Hook: the warband that wants you home.

traits.name: Mind Without Fog
traits.flavour: You were raised in a Lumeri cloister, or by priests of some other faith. Whatever you believe now, your mind is still water. Nobody has ever managed to stir it.
up: Still Water: you get 2 extra Attribute points at creation (12 instead of 10). Heart debuffs never affect you.
down: Unmoving: bonuses to Attributes and Skills from gear don't work on you, and your Karma can never change.

traits.name: The Brightest Light
traits.flavour: Burn it down, all of it. The brightest light burns out the fastest, and you've never cared how long you last.
up: Blaze: each enemy you take out in a fight gives you +10% damage for the rest of it, up to +50%.
down: Burnout: weapons wear out twice as fast in your hands. After every fight you took part in, you crash: −2 on every roll until you rest.

traits.name: Southern Fist
traits.flavour: You trained with the southern sects, where martial arts and magic were never separated. Your fists are weapons. Anything else in your hands is a clumsy stick.
up: These Hands: while you fight with nothing but gloves or bare fists, you have 1 more AP each turn and your unarmed strikes deal +20% damage.
down: Not That: every attack with any other weapon, guns included, costs 1 AP more.

traits.name: Forlorn Hope
traits.flavour: The Hellraiser storm units go in first and come back last, if they come back at all. You volunteered, and you'd volunteer again.
up: Charge: when you end your turn closer to the nearest enemy than you started it, you have 2 more AP on your next turn. Once every 3 turns.
down: No Way Back: armour above Class I gives you nothing more than Class I, and you can never Retreat or Disengage.

traits.name: Grenadier's Arm
traits.flavour: In the mess halls they arm-wrestle. In the field you throw: grenades, crates, Orks, the occasional squadmate.
up: Long Throw: +2 tiles of throwing range. You can also throw a person, a drone or an object next to you that weighs less than your carry weight, ally or enemy: it and whatever it lands on take damage that grows with its weight. Bosses can't be thrown.
down: Strained Arm: every throw costs 1 AP more.

traits.name: Glass Runner
traits.flavour: You were born on a low-gravity mining moon, and your bones never set right in real gravity. So you learned to move before anything could break them.
up: Runner: +5 Initiative, and your first move in each fight costs 1 AP less.
down: Glass: a critical hit that injures your arm or leg deals 50% more damage. A leg injury cuts your Movement to a quarter, not a half, until it is treated.

traits.name: Blade Recluse
traits.flavour: While your cohort at the academy drank and courted, you trained alone with one blade. Now the world is ending, and suddenly everyone wants to know you.
up: One Blade: outside a fight, name one weapon as yours. It can't be Disarmed and has one extra mod slot.
down: Rusty Manners: −1 Charisma, Insinuation and Authority. If anyone asks about your weapon, you tell them, at length; the Narrator holds you to it.

traits.name: Pain Eater
traits.flavour: Pain is the only thing that makes you sharp. Theirs or yours, it doesn't matter.
up: Bloodied: while you are below half your max HP, you deal +50% damage.
down: Fresh: while you are above half your max HP, you take +50% damage.

traits.name: Bottle Butts for Eyes
traits.flavour: Four-eyes, bookworm, glass-jaw. You've been called a lot of names, most of them accurate, but they didn't have to say it out loud.
up: Well-Read: +2 Rumination. You start with [Prescription Glasses]; while you wear them, +1 Acuity and Ingenuity.
down: Glasses Off: without them, −4 Acuity and Ingenuity. A critical hit to the head knocks them off (1 AP to put them back on in a fight), and the Narrator may knock them off in the story.

traits.name: The Mask
traits.flavour: Bare-faced, nobody looks at you twice. Put the mask on and the street parts for you.
up: Behind the Mask: you start with a [Smiling Mask]. While you wear it, +2 Composure and Authority. In a fight, putting it on or taking it off costs 1 AP.
down: Bare Face: without the mask, −3 Composure and Authority.
Two Faces: people who met you masked don't recognise you unmasked, and the other way round. The Narrator plays who knows which face.

traits.name: Machine-Faced
traits.flavour: You bought a new face at a back-alley clinic in Central City. It was a robot clinic. Nobody told the surgeon you weren't a robot.
up: Blank Face: every Composure check you make in a conversation succeeds without a roll. Robots and machines treat you as one of their own; the Narrator plays them.
down: Uncanny: you can't use Insinuation or Charisma in a conversation (their perks still work in a fight), and children and animals panic around you.

traits.name: Right of Way
traits.flavour: Central City's streets don't move aside for anyone, and neither do you. Your limp has been there since the old injury; you just walk through it.
up: I'm Walking Here: +2 Intimidation and Authority against anyone who blocks your path or interrupts you. You can't be Shoved.
down: Old Injury: −0.5 Movement and −2 Reaction Speed.

traits.name: Drill Echo
traits.flavour: Ten years ago you passed the academy's endurance drill with the best time in your cohort. The announcer's voice never stopped counting in your head.
up: Best Time: Sprint costs you 1 AP less, and your d20 can't roll below 10 on running, climbing and endurance checks.
down: The Count: whenever you concentrate (drawing a glyph, or a Brain Power or Rumination check), roll a d6. On a 1 the count starts again in your head: you lose the action and the AP it cost.

traits.name: The Old Blood
traits.flavour: You distrust anything unusual. You're conservative, and you don't want anything to change. Your own blood first, and only.
up: Bloodline: +2 Rumination and Guts. Among people of your own race and homeworld, +2 Authority.
down: Prejudice: with people of any other race, +2 Intimidation but −2 Charisma, Authority and Lore Master. Heals and Blessings from them work at half power on you, and you buy from them at +20% and sell to them at −20%.

traits.name: Holo-Drama Addict
traits.flavour: Three days without food, or three days without a holo-drama? You'd live on water.
up: Dramatic Timing: once per scene, describe your action as a scene from a holo-drama. If the Narrator buys the drama, you roll with +3. In a fight it needs no approval: your next attack that turn gets +3.
down: Leading Role: before anything unglamorous (crawling through sewage, hiding in a bin) you make a Visualization check (target 12) to picture it as a scene worth filming. On a fail you refuse, or do it at −3.

traits.name: Oil in My Mind
traits.flavour: Oil paint runs through the vessels of your brain. Give you a glass of wine and you could argue technique with Rémy Étienne or Master Sakamoto all night.
up: Canvas: study any artwork, mural, graffiti or designed object, and the Narrator tells you who made it, how, and where it came from. +1 Visualization, Acuity and Rumination.
down: Paper: −1 Durability, Pain Threshold and Senses, 2 less HP for each level, 10% more Elemental damage taken and 10% less healing received. If you have both Oil traits, you take this penalty only once.

traits.name: Oil in My Soul
traits.flavour: You don't know the technique. You know exactly how the painter felt.
up: Canvas: study any artwork, and the Narrator tells you what its maker felt and meant. +1 Empathy, Camaraderie and Insinuation.
down: Still Paper: −1 Durability, Pain Threshold and Senses, 2 less HP for each level, 10% more Elemental damage taken and 10% less healing received. If you have both Oil traits, you take this penalty only once.

traits.name: Lunarshine
traits.flavour: Part gentleman, part lush. A glass of Mandestra vintage, or the whole jug of lowland rotgut?
up: Tipsy (1 drink): +1 Camaraderie, Lore Master and Authority.
Drunk (3 drinks): a further +1 to those three, and +1 Intimidation, Guts and Durability.
down: Wasted (5 drinks): −2 Reaction Speed, Dexterity, Acuity, Vigilance, Improvisation and Visualization.

The Slope: a drink comes from a bottle of spirits in your pack and costs 1 AP in a fight. Drinks wear off at the end of each scene, but when a scene ends with you Drunk you make a Will Power check (target 12 + drinks today): on a fail you keep them and take one more. A day with no drink at all gives you the shakes: −1 Camaraderie, Authority and Composure until your next drink.

traits.name: Heavyworlder
traits.flavour: Born on a high-gravity world. Your mother has never forgiven you, the bullies at school never forgot you, and doorframes still don't fit you.
up: Dense: you count as one size larger. You can't be Shoved, your carry weight doubles, you can use heavy weapons one-handed, and you have +2 Intimidation.
down: Too Big: −3 Athletics and −0.5 Movement. Attacks against you have +2 to hit. You can't hide on a lit tile, you eat double rations, and vents, crawlspaces, small doors, lifts and light vehicles can't take you.

traits.name: Born Performer
traits.flavour: Every conversation is a stage, and you've never once been yourself on it. The world may not understand you, but you understand the world.
up: Adaptable: in each scene, one of your γ skills (the third skill of an Attribute) has +2. It starts on your highest one, and you may move it to another once per scene. +20% XP from combat.
down: Hollow: conversation never gives you XP, and anyone using Empathy on you gets +2: they sense nobody is home.

traits.name: Rabbit's Foot
traits.flavour: Half-Lapin by blood, or just someone who carries a rabbit's-foot charm. Either way, luck follows you, and so do the hunters.
up: Lucky Foot: once per session, the first enemy attack that would hit you in a fight is rerolled; you may hold it back for a later fight. Outside a fight, ask the Narrator to reroll one roll made against you.
Vengeful: when an ally is Downed, you have 2 more AP on your next turn. Once every 3 turns.
down: Prey: −1 Guts, Intimidation and Authority. Hunters and Orks deal +25% damage to you, and neither Take the Hit nor a taunt can pull their attacks off you.

traits.name: Ghost Soldier
traits.flavour: You fought in a war the records say never happened. The arm is new. The habits aren't.
up: Unseen: your first Ambush attack in each fight deals +50% damage and makes no sound. You start with a prosthetic arm that can take mods.
down: The War Never Ended: to rest in a settlement you must pass a Vigilance check (target 12), or you spend the night watching the doors and get nothing from the rest. When an enemy breaks your stealth, you have 2 AP less on your next turn. −1 Eloquence, Charisma, Insinuation and Composure.

traits.name: Symbol of Order
traits.flavour: The law is the only wall between the Thousand-Planet City and the dark. You are a stone in that wall.
up: I Am the Law: your Karma starts at Lawful. Once per scene, invoke the law or your rank: an official must answer one question truthfully. The Narrator plays the answer.
down: My Way: leaving Lawful costs double Karma, and every unlawful act you commit costs double Karma too.

traits.name: Rogue Element
traits.flavour: Plans, permits, chains of command: all of them break the same way, if you push hard enough.
up: Spanner in the Works: your Karma starts at Chaotic. Once per scene, when you wreck someone's plan or property, you gain 1 Echo. In a fight that means breaking an object; in the story the Narrator decides whether it counts.
down: My Way: leaving Chaotic costs double Karma. Lawful factions start hostile to you.

traits.name: The Soundscape of the Soul
traits.flavour: Gentle as a ripple, violent as a flood in the wet season, deep enough to drown your whole soul in.
up: Vibing: while your song plays, +1 to every Soul skill.
down: Lost the Vibe: when you have gone too long without your song, −1 to every Mind and Body skill.

traits.name: Headbanger
traits.flavour: The bass hits harder than a .700 Blackpoint round, and you want it louder.
up: Banger: while your song plays, +1 to every Body skill.
down: Losing It: when you have gone too long without your song, −1 to every Mind and Soul skill.

traits.name: Underground Sound
traits.flavour: Music while you sleep, cook, drive, even while you're listening to other music. And this band is criminally underrated.
up: Brain Dancing: while your song plays, +1 to every Mind skill.
down: Dead Air: when you have gone too long without your song, −1 to every Body and Soul skill.

traits.name: Worldline Fracture
traits.flavour: The worldlines are merging. Things that shouldn't exist walk your streets, and nobody else seems to notice.
up: Wild: the strangest, most impossible events turn up in your campaign. The Narrator chooses them.
down: Unravelling: those events replace the normal events of the area you are in.

traits.name: Factory Made
traits.flavour: Oil for blood, a plug for a gender, and a serial number for a name. The Factory built you to be spent. You weren't.
up: Machine Body: you are immune to poison, Bleeding and suffocation. Improvisation's Field Repair heals you like a machine, for 10 HP per point of Improvisation. With Improvisation 3 you can repair yourself: 2 AP and one spare-parts charge in a fight.
down: Plug: heals and Blessings work at half power on you, lightning and EMP deal double damage to you, and some humans won't talk to a machine.

traits.name: Lowland Born
traits.flavour: You grew up in the dead-building forest past the desert, Black Scavenger country, where every corner is an ambush.
up: Concrete Forest: in ruins and dense urban terrain, +1 Movement, and the Narrator always tells you one way out.
down: Open Sky: in open terrain, −2 Vigilance, and you spot Hidden enemies only within half your Vision range.

traits.name: Central City Kid
traits.flavour: Bank cards, shock batons, and somebody else to do the dirty work. Outside the walls, nobody is impressed.
up: Plugged In: you start with a city ID and a bank card. +2 on social checks with officials and merchants, and city services are open to you.
down: Soft Hands: the first time you lose HP in each fight, you lose 2 AP from the shock. Outside the city, −2 Guts.

traits.name: Daggerfall Veteran
traits.flavour: You were there. You remember what the speeches left out.
up: I Was There: you are immune to Fear, and once per fight you can remove one Heart debuff from yourself for 0 AP. +2 Authority and Composure with anyone military. Once per session, ask how the enemy will move next: in a fight you are shown each visible enemy's next move and target, and outside one the Narrator answers truthfully.
down: Flashback: once per fight, when you are Burning or an explosion goes off within 3 tiles of you, you make a Composure check (target 12) or lose your next turn. The Narrator can call for the same check in the story: shelling, burning, or a Crawler child.

traits.name: Upper-Touched
traits.flavour: You were born too close to the veil, and your twin soul in the upper realm talks back.
up: Thin Veil: your Outbursts cost 20% less mana, and you sense upper-realm beings within 10 tiles.
down: Seen From Above: upper-realm beings always know where you are, so you can't hide from them. Every Blessing cast on you rolls a d6 for a side effect: on a 1 it fails, on a 2 you gain 1 Strain, on a 3 you are Shaken for a round, on a 5 it is half again as strong, and on a 6 a voice from above speaks to you.

traits.name: Raised by Orks
traits.flavour: Your first word was a war-cry. Your second was the name of a weapon.
up: Ork Steel: +20% damage with melee weapons. Orks parley with you instead of attacking: an Ork won't attack you until your side attacks an Ork.
down: Can't Read: you can't use written documents or maps, and any check that needs reading fails. You have −2 Charisma with humans who know your history; each squadmate chooses whether that includes them.

traits.name: Gun Nut
traits.flavour: You can name the rifle from its echo and the factory from its casing.
up: Know Your Iron: you can name any firearm or round by its sound or casing: calibre, maker, where it was issued. Every gun you own has 1 extra mod slot, and clearing a jam costs you 0 AP.
down: Collector: the first 3 guns you get are your collection (your kit's gun counts), and you always carry them, weight included. To sell, abandon or give away one of them you must pass a Dexterity check (target 12): the gun hand has to let go. On a fail, you can't part with it until your next rest. You sell every gun at half price: you never really want to let go.

traits.name: Old School
traits.flavour: The drifter's creed: identify, squeeze, breathe the powder smoke, dig the grave.
up: Fan the Hammer: once per turn, with a revolver or lever gun, spend 3 AP to fire every round still loaded at one target. Each shot is at −2 to hit, and Recoil builds from shot to shot.
down: Analog: you can't use electronic or Evoker-linked guns, or a red dot sight.

traits.name: Spray and Pray
traits.flavour: The Hellraiser doctrine: volume of fire is a tactic.
up: Suppression: every target your full-auto burst fires at, hit or miss, makes a Body save or is Suppressed: 1 AP less on its next turn, and no reactions or Overwatch. It doesn't stack. Your full-auto penalty is −1 instead of −2.
down: Ammo Hog: every round you fire uses up two, and your aimed shots are at −2 to hit.

traits.name: One Shot
traits.flavour: Breathe out. Squeeze. Don't look away.
up: Breath Held: if you haven't moved this turn, your first shot ignores half cover and deals +25% Critical Damage (a critical is never more than double damage).
down: Tunnel Vision: after that shot, until you next move, your Vigilance checks fail, you can't spot Hidden enemies, and Ambushes deal +50% damage to you.

traits.name: Sigil Savant
traits.flavour: Twenty years at the Science Team bench, and one Sigil you can draw in your sleep.
up: Muscle Memory: choose one Sigil word. Drawing its glyph always costs you 0 Core charge and 1 AP less (never below half an AP).
down: Rigid: you can only draw the words you practised at your last long rest (as many as your Max Sigil words), plus your Muscle Memory word. Nothing new mid-mission.

traits.name: Hollow Heart
traits.flavour: A Mana Short left a hole in your chest. The fear went out through it.
up: Hollow: when the burn of your own Strain Downs you, you are unconscious but stable: you make no death saves, and hits don't count against you. A Mana Short doesn't Stun you. +10% Outburst damage.
down: Echo Chamber: every Outburst you cast is loud. Every enemy within 10 tiles learns where you are, and you can't be Hidden on a turn you cast.

traits.name: Heretic
traits.flavour: You learned to call down a Blessing without kneeling to anyone. The saints noticed.
up: Stolen Fire: you can pray for any patron's Blessings without Faith and without a pact. Your Will Power takes the place of Faith for everything a Blessing asks, its power included. A stolen Hymn is rolled: d20 + Will Power against 14, 16 or 18 by the Hymn's tier (outside a fight it needs Will Power 3).
down: Excommunicated: every faith-based faction is hostile to you, the Lumeri Church first. A Blessing an ally casts on you fails on a 1–2 on a d6.

traits.name: Gambler
traits.flavour: The house always wins. You are not the house, and you've never once let that stop you.
up: Double or Nothing: once per scene, call "double" before a d20 check or attack roll. A success becomes a critical success; a failure becomes a critical failure.
down: In Debt: you owe the Smetanita Conjunction. Their collectors turn up when the Narrator decides.

traits.name: Insomniac
traits.flavour: Sleep is for people without a watch rotation.
up: Always Up: you can't be ambushed while the squad rests, and you take a watch with no penalty.
down: Wired: a rest restores only half as much HP and mana for you.

traits.name: Chain Smoker
traits.flavour: Smoke break. Now. The Orks can wait.
up: Light Up: spend 2 AP in a fight or on the area map (free in the story) to gain +2 Composure for the scene and remove one Heart debuff from yourself.
down: Hacking Cough: −1 Athletics. Enemies smell you coming: +2 to their Detection against you.

traits.name: Live to Fight Another Day
traits.flavour: Brave is a word they carve on headstones.
up: Tactical Withdrawal: once per turn, Disengage costs you 0 AP. Once per fight, you can Retreat for 0 AP: a Sprint that ends farther from every enemy you can see and draws no opportunity attacks. Either one gives you +2 Defense until the end of your next turn.
down: Yellow: allies within 3 tiles of you take −1 on saves against Fear. It's contagious.

traits.name: Sworn Sibling
traits.flavour: Blood, oath, or something stronger. Where they go, you go.
up: Bound: bond with one squadmate; their player has to agree. Each round the two of you start a turn next to each other, one of you gets 1 free AP. You always know where they are, even through walls.
down: Bound: if they go down, you must reach them. Until you are next to them, your attacks are at −2 unless they defend your sibling (an enemy within 2 tiles of them, or one that hurt them), your skill checks are at −2 unless they are for your sibling, and a move that ends farther from them costs double AP. Your HP, damage and other combat stats aren't affected.

traits.name: Rival
traits.flavour: Jealous? Why would you be jealous? Completely ridiculous.
up: Show-Off: bond with one squadmate as your rival; their player has to agree. After your rival succeeds with a skill, your next roll with that same skill gets +2.

Neck and Neck: whenever your rival reaches a new level, you gain 50 XP. While your rival is a higher level than you, you get +10% XP from every source except Essence. It works both ways: your rival gets the same from you.
down: Petty: before you help your rival (handing them AP, healing them, giving them cover) you must pass a Camaraderie check (target 12). On a fail you can't help them that turn.

traits.name: Humanity First
traits.flavour: The stars belong to humankind. Robots are tools, Crawlers are vermin, and anything from the upper realm is the enemy.
up: For Humanity: +15% damage against non-humans (robots, Crawlers, Orks, upper-realm beings) and +2 on saves against their Fear effects.
down: Xenophobe: you can't use Empathy, Charisma or Camaraderie with non-humans. Non-human squadmates can't hand you AP, and their heals work at half power on you.

traits.name: Wanted
traits.flavour: Your face is on a poster in every Central City precinct, and it's a bad likeness.
up: Notorious: +2 Intimidation with the underworld. You start with one piece of contraband.
down: Bounty: bounty hunters appear when the Narrator decides, and Central City officials start hostile to you and your squad.

traits.name: Company Man
traits.flavour: Rigaz Trade Company (RTC™®). The card has no limit. The contract does.
up: Company Card: RTC sells you its gear at cost, 40% off the list price. Once per campaign, call RTC to extract you from anywhere. In a fight you leave it and earn no XP from it; the Narrator decides where you land.
down: Contract: RTC sends you jobs. You can't refuse one without breaking the contract, and RTC remembers.

traits.name: Field Medic
traits.flavour: You learned triage under fire, in a medical unit where the casualty rate was the point.
up: Triage: healing an ally costs you 1 AP less, never below 1 AP. Once per fight, you can throw a stim to stabilise a Downed ally up to 3 tiles away that you can see.
down: First, Do No Harm: if an ally within 5 tiles is below a quarter of their HP when your turn starts, you can't attack that turn until you have healed someone. This only binds you while you have a way to heal.

traits.name: Squad Anchor
traits.flavour: Someone has to hold the line so everyone else can move.
up: Hold Fast: allies within 2 tiles of you get +1 on all saves and +1 Defense. If you haven't moved this turn, the range is 3 tiles.
down: Fixed Point: on a turn when you move more than 2 tiles, the effect stops until your next turn, and you have 1 AP less on that turn.

traits.name: Born Officer
traits.flavour: A commission, a bloodline, or just the voice. When you speak, soldiers move.
up: Command: once per round, spend 1 AP to give an ally you can see a free 1 AP move or a free basic attack. Your Leadership rating counts one step higher.
down: The Squad Leans on You: an ally within 5 tiles of you starts their turn with 1 AP less if you are Downed or they can't see you. Taking an order from anyone else takes a Composure check.

traits.name: Cold Case
traits.flavour: The CCEC washed you out, or you walked. Either way, you never stopped working cases.
up: Case File: Analyze costs you 1 AP less. Once per session, after you investigate a scene, ask the Narrator one yes-or-no question about whoever is responsible. The answer is true.
down: Obsession: while a case is open, −1 on every roll in scenes that have nothing to do with it. The Narrator opens and closes your cases.

traits.name: Interrogator
traits.flavour: Central Command taught you the quiet room. You still know where every bone in the hand is.
up: The Quiet Room: alone with a captive, +2 Intimidation and Eloquence. A captive you break gives you one true answer they would never give anyone else; the Narrator plays it.
down: Known Trade: with civilians who learn what you do, you have −2 Charisma and Empathy.

traits.name: Trench Poet
traits.flavour: You can't say anything plainly. Plain words are for orders and obituaries.
up: Verse: once per scene, answer in metaphor to one listener within 8 tiles; in a fight it costs 1 AP. The listener makes a Heart save against your Insinuation or is Confused. Allies who hear you get +1 Composure for the scene.
down: Nothing Straight: giving a plain, direct answer takes an Eloquence check; the Narrator calls for it.

traits.name: Grudge Bearer
traits.flavour: You remember every slight. You've written most of them down.
up: Spite: debuffs you inflict last 1 round longer, except Stunned and Dazed. The first one you inflict in each fight skips the target's save, unless the target is a boss or the debuff is Stunned.
down: Never Forgive: when someone wrongs you, the Narrator marks them. Until you get even, −2 on every roll that isn't aimed at them.

traits.name: Crowded Head
traits.flavour: Every skill in your head has an opinion, and none of them wait their turn.
up: Chorus: you hear up to 4 voice lines per story beat instead of 2, and you can Ask a skill twice per scene instead of once.
down: Cacophony: resisting an Overreach costs you 1 more Echo, and once per session the Narrator may make one of your voice lines misleading, even when that voice knew the truth.

traits.name: Market Blood
traits.flavour: You grew up behind a stall in Mandestra. You can price a man by his boots.
up: Haggle: you buy at −20% and sell at +20%. Touch any item to learn its true value, and whether it is a fake.
down: Price on Everything: giving away an item or accepting a gift takes an Acuity check, because you can't stop pricing it; the Narrator calls for it. −1 Camaraderie.

traits.name: Cover Story
traits.flavour: You've sold the same bridge in four systems, under four names.
up: New Name: once per session, set up a false identity in one sentence. People accept it until you fail a roll in front of them.
down: Paper Trail: the Narrator counts every identity you burn. At 3, someone from an old con turns up.

traits.name: Inner Ring Heir
traits.flavour: Old money from Central City's inner ring. Your family name opens doors, and paints a target.
up: Allowance: you start with triple funds. Once per session, call in a favour from the family; the Narrator decides what it gets you.
down: The Name: every enemy of your house knows you, kidnappers included, and you can't refuse a family summons.

traits.name: Slicer
traits.flavour: You started out cracking bank cards in Central City. You graduated to doors, cameras and turrets.
up: Backdoor: spend 2 AP to take control of one electronic device within 5 tiles (a door, terminal, camera, alarm or emplaced turret) until your next turn. It takes an Acuity check against the device's tier.
down: Jacked In: because of your implant, any EMP or lightning hit Stuns you for 1 turn, and machines get +2 to their Detection against you.

traits.name: Demolitionist
traits.flavour: Every problem is a load-bearing wall.
up: Shaped Charge: spend 2 AP to set one of your explosives on your tile or the one next to you, and choose the blast's shape: a line, a cone or a circle. Set it off at once, or later with Detonate for 1 AP. +30% explosive damage.
down: Ringing Ears: −2 Vigilance, and any check that depends on hearing fails.

traits.name: Drone Handler
traits.flavour: It's small, it's loud, and it's the only one in the squad that never complains.
up: Little Friend: you start with a drone that acts right after you, with 30 HP and 3 AP of its own. It scouts for the squad or carries 5 kg, and you repair it with Improvisation.
down: Tethered: if the drone is destroyed, you are Shaken until you rebuild it, which takes a rest and materials.

traits.name: Augmented
traits.flavour: Part of you came out of a catalogue.
up: Chrome: pick one augment at creation. Arm: +20% Physical damage with weapons. Eye: +2 Vision range, and you see in darkness. Legs: +1 Movement, and you can jump up to 2 tiles, over a blocked one.
down: Maintenance: after each rest you make an Improvisation check (target 12); on a fail, the augment doesn't work until your next rest. An EMP hit switches it off for 2 turns.

traits.name: True Believer
traits.flavour: Holy Father Nerukhan, or some other saint, has never once let you down. You've never once let them down either.
up: Unshaken: the wait between your Hymns is 1 round shorter, never under 2 rounds. Once per session, ask for a small miracle: the Narrator grants it.
down: Rites: keep your church's daily rites (dawn prayer, fasting days). For each day you can't, −1 Faith and Will Power, up to −3, until you make amends.

traits.name: Heaven's Faithful
traits.flavour: The Department fights Heaven. You pray to it. If they ever find out, they'll shoot you.
up: Communion: once per scene, outside a fight, ask your twin soul in the upper realm one question. The Narrator answers truthfully, but in riddles. +2 Outburst range.
down: Treason: if the Department learns your faith, you are hunted. At the start of each fight against upper-realm beings you make a Faith check (target 12); on a fail you hesitate and lose 2 AP on your first turn.

traits.name: Occultist
traits.flavour: The Institute of Forgotten Knowledge lent you one book. You never gave it back.
up: Forbidden Text: you start with a grimoire. Once per session, look up a supernatural creature: the Narrator tells you its weakness. Outside a fight, you can spend 10 minutes warding an area against the supernatural.
down: Overdue: the Institute wants its book back. The book talks too: once per session, the Narrator whispers you one false line through it.

traits.name: Crawler-Blooded
traits.flavour: Your grandmother crossed the line at Daggerfall. Her blood still shows under your skin.
up: Chitin: a critical hit that injures your arm or leg deals 30% less damage. You can climb walls at half Movement where the Narrator allows it, and a Crawler never attacks you until you attack a Crawler.
down: Marked: humans who see your blood start hostile. A Blessing from a Lumeri patron burns you for 10 damage before it takes effect.

traits.name: Old Timer
traits.flavour: You were already old when Daggerfall happened.
up: Seen It All: you start each session with 1 extra Echo (2 in all). Once per session, outside a fight, declare you have seen this before: one Rumination, Lore Master or Acuity check succeeds automatically.
down: Old Bones: −0.5 Movement and −10% max HP. After a night without a full rest, −2 on every Body skill the next day.

traits.name: Pacifist
traits.flavour: You won't kill. Not even them.
up: Sanctuary: until you attack in a fight, enemies have −2 to hit you. Your attacks are nonlethal unless you choose otherwise: an enemy you would have killed is subdued instead, and you get +3 on checks to talk to it afterwards. Mercy earns you double Karma.
down: The Vow: if you kill, you lose all your Echo and are Shaken for the rest of the session.

traits.name: Moon Hunter
traits.flavour: You tracked game across three moons before you ever tracked a man.
up: Tracker: you can follow any trail less than a day old; the Narrator tells you where it leads. Your first attack on a creature you tracked this scene deals +30% damage (a miss uses it up too).
down: Wild Born: in cities, −2 Charisma, Eloquence and Authority.

traits.name: Beast Handler
traits.flavour: It came to you half-starved. Now it would die for you, and nearly has.
up: Companion: a trained beast fights at your side and acts right after you, with 60 HP, 4 AP of its own and a bite that can Grapple. Each turn it obeys you on an Empathy check; on a fail it acts on instinct.
down: Bond: if it dies, you are Shaken for the rest of the campaign arc. It can't enter most buildings in Central City.

traits.name: Ace Pilot
traits.flavour: Give you anything with an engine and you'll find out what it can really do.
up: Born Behind the Stick: you can drive or pilot anything with an engine, with no check. Vehicles you drive get +1 Movement and use your Dodge; the Narrator runs them.
down: Grounded: after a full day on foot when there were vehicles to be had, −0.5 Movement and −1 Reaction Speed until you are back in a seat. The Narrator decides when that applies.

body: Muscle, blood, and how well you command your own flesh.
Runs on ammo, weapons and tech
mind: The brain: absorbing theory and thinking logically.
Burns mana cores to draw Sigils
soul: The heart: emotional awareness and social perception.
Spends mana on Soul spells and prayer

ults.name: War Footing
ults.flavour: The Hellraisers call it marching on the enemy's nerves.
ults.text: Your threats never backfire: a failed Intimidation check costs you nothing, though you can't try again on the same person that scene. An enemy that ends a move next to you loses 2 AP at once, unless it Disengaged. Once every 3 turns.

ults.name: Last Charge
ults.flavour: Every army has a song for running at guns. You know all of them.
ults.text: When you charge 5 or more tiles in a straight line at an enemy, your melee hits deal ×1.5 damage for the rest of that turn. Once per fight, that charge also gives you a shield of 15 × your Armour Class (at least 15) until your next turn starts.

ults.name: Angel of the Trenches
ults.flavour: The 258th Medical Unit's highest honour has no medal. The soldiers just say your name.
ults.text: Once per fight, when an ally you could reach with 1 AP of movement would drop to 0 HP, you run to them out of turn for 0 AP and stabilise them: they stay up at 1 HP and stop Bleeding. The run draws no opportunity attacks. Choose Hold position on your turn if you would rather stay put.

ults.name: Every Lie Is a Door
ults.flavour: You don't break in. You get invited.
ults.text: Once per session, walk into any guarded place by naming a reason to be there. You alone are believed, and its guards don't notice you sneaking, until a weapon is drawn, a fight starts or the scene ends. The Narrator plays the people you meet.

ults.name: Twin Discipline
ults.flavour: The Science Team says it can't be done. The Institute says it shouldn't be. You do it anyway.
ults.text: While you hold a begun Outburst, Evoke a Sigil Line as one fused cast. The Sigil's words set where it reaches and what it covers; the Outburst sets the school and the stage, and each creature it covers takes it as a Bolt. You pay both costs.

ults.name: Supreme Command
ults.flavour: Five stars, and nobody looks you in the eye.
ults.text: Once per fight, on your turn, give one order to the whole squad for 0 AP. Every other conscious squadmate takes one action of up to 2 AP at once, for free.
